sentences.zh: 宋一鶴，宛平人。

translations.literal: Song Yihe was a native of Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yihe was from Wanping.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，見天下大亂，即究心兵事。

translations.literal: As a licentiate, seeing the realm in great disorder, he at once devoted himself to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While still a licentiate, he saw the empire falling into chaos and threw himself into the study of war.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in Chongzhen 3.

sentences.zh: 授教諭，以薦遷丘縣知縣，復以薦加東昌同知，仍知縣事。

translations.literal: He was appointed instructor; on recommendation he was transferred to magistrate of Qiu County, and again on recommendation was made Tongzhi of Dongchang while still carrying out the duties of county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an instructor, then recommended up to magistrate of Qiu County, and recommended again to serve as vice-prefect of Dongchang while continuing to administer the county.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史禹好善以一鶴知兵，薦之。

translations.literal: The touring censor Yu Haoshan, because Yihe understood military affairs, recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Yu Haoshan recommended him on the ground that Yihe knew warfare.

sentences.zh: 授兵部員外郎，尋擢天津兵備僉事，改飭汝南兵備，駐信陽。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director in the Ministry of War, and soon was promoted to vice commissioner for military preparations at Tianjin; he was then reassigned to oversee military preparations in Runan and stationed at Xinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a vice director in the Ministry of War, soon promoted to vice commissioner for Tianjin military preparations, then reassigned to oversee Runan defenses and stationed at Xinyang.

sentences.zh: 時熊文燦總理南畿、河南、山西、陜西、湖廣、四川軍務，主撫議。

translations.literal: At the time Xiong Wencan was grand coordinator of military affairs for the Southern Metropolitan Region, Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Huguang, and Sichuan, and upheld the policy of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Wencan then directed military affairs across the southern capital region, Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Huguang, and Sichuan, and favored a conciliatory policy toward the rebels.

sentences.zh: 一鶴降其盜魁黃三耀，又降其死賊順天王之黨劉喜才。

translations.literal: Yihe induced the bandit chieftain Huang Sanyao to surrender, and also induced Liu Xicai, a follower of the dead bandit Shuntianwang, to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yihe induced the bandit leader Huang Sanyao to submit, and likewise won over Liu Xicai, a follower of the slain rebel known as Shuntianwang.

sentences.zh: 一鶴先後剿劇賊，斬首七百有奇。

translations.literal: Yihe in succession suppressed fierce bandits and beheaded more than seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In successive campaigns against major rebel bands he took more than seven hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 從副將龍在田破賊固始，一鶴毒殺其賊千人。

translations.literal: Following the vice general Long Zaitian in defeating bandits at Gushi, Yihe by poison killed a thousand of their bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He followed vice general Long Zaitian in defeating rebels at Gushi, and himself poisoned a thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 左良玉降其賊李萬慶，一鶴撫而定之數萬。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu induced the bandit Li Wanqing to surrender; Yihe pacified and settled several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After Zuo Liangyu induced the rebel Li Wanqing to surrender, Yihe pacified and settled tens of thousands of his followers.

sentences.zh: 文燦屢上其功，薦之，進副使，調鄖陽。

translations.literal: Wencan repeatedly reported his achievements and recommended him; he was advanced to vice commissioner and transferred to Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan repeatedly memorialized his achievements and had him promoted to vice commissioner and transferred to Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 文燦誅，楊嗣昌代，以一鶴能，薦之，擢右僉都御史，代方孔炤巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: When Wencan was executed, Yang Sichang replaced him; because Yihe was capable, he recommended him, and Yihe was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and replaced Fang Kongzhao as grand coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wencan was put to death, Yang Sichang succeeded him; impressed by Yihe's ability, he recommended him for promotion to right vice censor-in-chief and appointment as grand coordinator of Huguang in place of Fang Kongzhao.

sentences.zh: 時湖廣賊為諸將所逼，多竄入四川。

translations.literal: At the time the bandits of Huguang, pressed by the various generals, for the most part fled into Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Huguang rebels, harried by the field commanders, were mostly slipping into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 一鶴以雲南軍移鎮當陽，中官劉元斌以京軍移鎮荊門，相掎角。

translations.literal: Yihe moved the Yunnan army to garrison Dangyang, and the eunuch Liu Yuanbin moved the capital army to garrison Jingmen, the two supporting each other in pincer fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Yihe shifted the Yunnan troops to hold Dangyang while the eunuch Liu Yuanbin moved capital troops to Jingmen, the two posts working in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 左良玉等大破賊於瑪瑙山，一鶴敘功增俸。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu and others inflicted a great defeat on the bandits at Mount Manao; Yihe had his merit recorded and his salary increased.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu and others routed the rebels at Mount Manao, and Yihe's rewards were entered on the rolls with an increase in salary.

sentences.zh: 遣副將王允成、孫應元等大破賊汝才五大營於豐邑坪，斬首三千余級。

translations.literal: He sent the vice generals Wang Yuncheng and Sun Yingyuan and others to inflict a great defeat on the five great camps of the bandit Rucai at Fengyiping, beheading more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He sent vice generals Wang Yuncheng and Sun Yingyuan and others to crush the five main camps of the rebel Rucai at Fengyiping, taking more than three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌署一鶴荊楚第一功。

translations.literal: Sichang ranked Yihe's achievement first in Jing-Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang credited Yihe with the foremost achievement in the Jing-Chu theater.

sentences.zh: 獻忠陷襄陽，與革裏眼、左金王等東萃黃州、汝寧間。

translations.literal: Xianzhong took Xiangyang and, with Geli Yan, Zuo Jinwang, and others, gathered eastward between Huangzhou and Runing.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong seized Xiangyang and, with Geli Yan, Zuo Jinwang, and others, massed east of the line between Huangzhou and Runing.

sentences.zh: 一鶴移駐蘄州，焚舟，遏賊渡。

translations.literal: Yihe moved his headquarters to Qizhou, burned the boats, and blocked the bandits' crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Yihe shifted his headquarters to Qizhou, burned the boats, and blocked the rebels from crossing the river.

sentences.zh: 賊移而北，一鶴又斷橫江，賊不敢渡。

translations.literal: The bandits shifted northward; Yihe again cut the crossing at Hengjiang, and the bandits did not dare cross.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels moved north, Yihe again blocked the Hengjiang crossing and they did not dare attempt a passage.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌卒，丁啟睿代。

translations.literal: Sichang died, and Ding Qirui replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After Sichang died, Ding Qirui took his place.

sentences.zh: 啟睿破獻忠於麻城，會一鶴及鳳陽總督朱大典、安慶巡撫鄭二陽蹙賊左金王、老回回等於潛山、懷寧山中。

translations.literal: Qirui defeated Xianzhong at Macheng; joining with Yihe and the Fengyang governor Zhu Dadian and the Anqing grand coordinator Zheng Eryang, he pressed the bandits Zuo Jinwang, Lao Huihui, and others in the mountains of Qianshan and Huaining.
translations.idiomatic: Qirui defeated Xianzhong at Macheng, then joined Yihe, Fengyang governor Zhu Dadian, and Anqing grand coordinator Zheng Eryang in driving Zuo Jinwang, Lao Huihui, and others into the Qianshan and Huaining hills.

sentences.zh: 一鶴又督參將王嘉謨等追破左金王、爭世王、治世王於燈草坪，斬首千八百級。

translations.literal: Yihe again supervised the brigade generals Wang Jiamo and others in pursuing and defeating Zuo Jinwang, Zhengshiwang, and Zhishiwang at Dengcaoping, beheading one thousand eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Yihe then directed brigade generals including Wang Jiamo in a pursuit that broke Zuo Jinwang, Zhengshiwang, and Zhishiwang at Dengcaoping, taking eighteen hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遣部將陳治等合江北兵，破賊於桐城、舒城。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he sent his subordinate generals Chen Zhi and others to join with the troops north of the Yangzi and defeat the bandits at Tongcheng and Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen he sent subordinates such as Chen Zhi to combine with troops north of the Yangzi and defeat the rebels at Tongcheng and Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 一鶴起鄉舉，不十年秉節鉞，廷臣不能無忮。

translations.literal: Yihe had risen from the provincial examination; in less than ten years he wielded military authority, and court officials could not be without jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Yihe had entered service through the provincial examinations and within a decade held military command; courtiers could hardly avoid envy.

sentences.zh: 御史衛周允上疏醜詆一鶴。

translations.literal: The censor Wei Zhouyun submitted a memorial vilifying Yihe.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Zhouyun memorialized the throne with a vicious attack on Yihe.

sentences.zh: 一鶴屢建功，然亦往往蒙時詬。

translations.literal: Yihe repeatedly achieved merit, yet he also often bore the reproaches of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yihe won repeated victories, he was just as often caught up in the controversies of the day.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌父名鶴，一鶴投揭，自署其名曰「一鳥」，楚人傳笑之。

translations.literal: Sichang's father's name was He; Yihe submitted a petition and signed his own name as "One Bird," and the people of Chu passed the story around in laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang's father had been named He, so when Yihe submitted a memorial he signed himself "One Bird" instead of "One Crane," and the people of Chu made a laughingstock of it.

sentences.zh: 一鶴亦連疏引疾，帝疑其偽，下所司嚴核。

translations.literal: Yihe also repeatedly memorialized citing illness; the emperor suspected it was feigned and ordered the responsible offices to investigate strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Yihe too sent repeated memorials pleading illness; the emperor suspected pretense and ordered a strict inquiry by the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 先以襄陽陷，奪職戴罪，至是許解官候代。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Xiangyang had fallen, his office had been removed and he bore guilt; now he was permitted to resign and await a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been stripped of rank and left to atone after the fall of Xiangyang; now he was allowed to resign and wait for a successor.

sentences.zh: 趨救汝寧，汝寧城已陷。

translations.literal: He hurried to relieve Runing, but the city of Runing had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to relieve Runing only to find the city already lost.

sentences.zh: 十二月，襄陽、德安、荊州連告陷，一鶴趨承天護獻陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Xiangyang, De'an, and Jingzhou in succession reported fallen; Yihe hurried to Chengtian to protect the Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month came word that Xiangyang, De'an, and Jingzhou had fallen in turn; Yihe raced to Chengtian to defend the Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 陵軍柵木為城，賊積薪燒之，煙窨純德山。

translations.literal: The mausoleum troops palisaded timber into a wall; the bandits heaped fuel and burned it, and smoke shrouded Mount Chunde.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison threw up a timber palisade; the rebels piled fuel against it and set it ablaze until smoke wrapped Mount Chunde.

sentences.zh: 城穿，一鼓而登，犯獻陵，毀禋殿。

translations.literal: The wall was breached; with one drumbeat they mounted it, violated the Xian Mausoleum, and destroyed the sacrificial hall.
translations.idiomatic: Once the defenses gave way they scaled the wall at a single rush, entered the mausoleum precinct, and wrecked the main sacrificial hall.

sentences.zh: 守陵巡按御史李振聲、總兵官錢中選皆降，遂攻承天，歲除，明年正月二日，有以城下賊者。

translations.literal: The mausoleum-guarding touring censor Li Zhensheng and the commander-in-chief Qian Zhongxuan both surrendered; then they attacked Chengtian. On New Year's Eve, on the second day of the first month of the following year, there was someone who led the bandits into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Li Zhensheng and commander Qian Zhongxuan, charged with guarding the mausoleum, both surrendered; the rebels then turned on Chengtian. On New Year's Eve and the second day of the first month of the new year, someone inside opened the gates to them.

sentences.zh: 城陷，一鶴自經，故留守沈壽崇、鐘祥知縣蕭漢俱死，分巡副使張鳳翥走入山中。

translations.literal: The city fell; Yihe hanged himself. The former garrison commander Shen Shoucong and the Zhongxiang magistrate Xiao Han both died; the vice commissioner for circuit administration Zhang Fengzhu fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Yihe hanged himself. Former garrison commander Shen Shoucong and Zhongxiang magistrate Xiao Han died with him, while circuit vice commissioner Zhang Fengzhu escaped into the hills.

sentences.zh: 先是左良玉軍擾襄、樊，一鶴疏糾之。

translations.literal: Earlier Zuo Liangyu's army had harassed Xiang and Fan; Yihe memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zuo Liangyu's troops had been ravaging Xiangyang and Fancheng, Yihe had memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 既，良玉自襄走承天，軍饑而掠，乞餉於一鶴，不許。

translations.literal: Afterward Liangyu fled from Xiang to Chengtian; his army, hungry, plundered and begged provisions from Yihe, who would not grant them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liangyu withdrew from Xiangyang toward Chengtian; his hungry troops looted the countryside and asked Yihe for pay, which he refused.

sentences.zh: 良玉銜之。

translations.literal: Liangyu bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu never forgave the slight.

sentences.zh: 至是，一鶴謀留良玉兵，良玉走武昌，故及於難。

translations.literal: At this time Yihe planned to retain Liangyu's troops, but Liangyu fled to Wuchang; therefore he met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yihe hoped to keep Liangyu's force at hand, but Liangyu marched off to Wuchang instead, leaving Yihe to face the calamity alone.

sentences.zh: 壽崇，宣城人，都督有容子。

translations.literal: Shoucong was a native of Xuancheng, son of the regional commander You Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucong, a native of Xuancheng, was the son of regional commander You Rong.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初武進士。

translations.literal: In the early Chongzhen reign he became a military jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He took his military jinshi degree early in the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 忤巡按，被劾罷，未行而賊至，遂及於難。

translations.literal: He offended the touring censor, was impeached and dismissed, and before he could depart the bandits arrived; thus he met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He had clashed with a touring censor, been impeached, and was on the point of leaving when the rebels arrived and he perished in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 贈都督僉事，蔭子錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of vice regional commander, and his son was granted the hereditary office of commander of one hundred households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made vice regional commander, and his son was ennobled as a hereditary commander of one hundred households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 漢，字雲濤，南豐人。

translations.literal: Han, styled Yuntao, was a native of Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Han, whose courtesy name was Yuntao, came from Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Chongzhen 10.

sentences.zh: 秩滿將行，賊薄城，即辭家廟，授帨於妾媵曰：「男忠女烈，努力自盡。

translations.literal: When his term was complete and he was about to depart, bandits pressed the city; he at once took leave at the family shrine and handed his sash to a concubine, saying: "Let the men be loyal and the women steadfast; strive to end your lives yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: As his term ended and he prepared to leave, rebels closed on the city; he went straight to the family shrine and gave his sash to a concubine, saying, "Let the men be loyal and the women resolute—do your utmost to die with honor.

sentences.zh: 」遂出登陴，拒守五晝夜。

translations.literal: " He then went out and mounted the ramparts, holding out for five days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he went out to the walls and held the city for five days and nights.

sentences.zh: 元旦，突圍出，趨獻陵。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day he broke out of the encirclement and hurried toward the Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day he fought his way out and rushed toward the Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 賊騎環之，漢大呼：「鐘祥令在，誰敢驚陵寢者！

translations.literal: Bandit horsemen surrounded him; Han shouted loudly: "The magistrate of Zhongxiang is here—who dares disturb the imperial tombs!
translations.idiomatic: Rebel horsemen ringed him about; Han cried out, "The magistrate of Zhongxiang is here—who dares disturb the royal tombs!

sentences.zh: 」賊挾之去，不殺，說降，不聽。

translations.literal: " The bandits seized him and took him away without killing him; they urged him to surrender, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels seized him but did not kill him; they urged him to submit, and he refused.

sentences.zh: 明日，城陷，送漢吉祥寺，謹視之，求死不得。

translations.literal: The next day the city fell; they sent Han to Jixiang Temple and watched him closely; he sought death but could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the city fell; they took Han to Jixiang Temple and kept him under close guard so that he could not find a way to die.

sentences.zh: 越三日，從僧榻得剃刀，藏之，取敝紙書楊繼盛絕命詞，紙盡，投筆起，復拾土塊畫「鐘祥縣令蕭漢願死此寺」十字於壁，即對壁自剄，血正濺字上，死矣。

translations.literal: After three days he obtained a razor from a monk's couch, hid it, took scrap paper and wrote Yang Jisheng's final verses; when the paper was exhausted he threw down the brush and rose, then picked up a clod of earth and wrote on the wall the ten characters "Zhongxiang Magistrate Xiao Han wishes to die in this temple"; facing the wall he cut his own throat, and blood splashed directly upon the characters—he was dead.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he found a razor by a monk's pallet, hid it, and on scraps of paper copied Yang Jisheng's death poem; when the paper ran out he threw down the brush, took up a lump of earth, and wrote on the wall, "Zhongxiang Magistrate Xiao Han wishes to die in this temple." He then faced the wall and cut his throat; the blood fell squarely on the characters, and he died.

sentences.zh: 賊嘉其義，用錦衣斂而瘞之。

translations.literal: The bandits admired his righteousness and buried him in brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels admired his integrity and buried him in silken robes.

sentences.zh: 賊退，其門人改斂之以時服，曰：「嗚呼，大白其無黷乎！

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, his disciples reburied him in the proper garments of the time, saying: "Alas, would the Great White Star be without impurity!
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels withdrew, his disciples reburied him in proper dress, saying, "Would the Great White Star suffer defilement!

sentences.zh: 吾師肯服賊服乎！

translations.literal: Would our teacher consent to wear the garments of bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Would our teacher have worn rebel garb!

sentences.zh: 」悉易之。

translations.literal: " They changed them all.
translations.idiomatic: They replaced every article of the rebel burial.

sentences.zh: 詔贈漢大理寺丞。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted Han the post of vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 振聲，米脂人。

translations.literal: Zhensheng was a native of Mizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhensheng was from Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 與自成同縣而同姓，自成呼之為兄，後復殺之。

translations.literal: He was from the same county and bore the same surname as Zicheng; Zicheng called him elder brother, but later killed him again.
translations.idiomatic: He shared Zicheng's county and surname; Zicheng called him elder brother, yet later had him killed.

sentences.zh: 將發獻陵，大聲起山谷，若雷震虎嗥，懼，乃止。

translations.literal: When they were about to despoil the Xian Mausoleum, a great sound rose from the valleys like thunder and the roaring of tigers; in fear they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to plunder the mausoleum, a great noise rolled through the valleys like thunder and tiger roars; terrified, they desisted.

sentences.zh: 馮師孔，字景魯，原武人。

translations.literal: Feng Shikong, styled Jinglu, was a native of Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shikong, courtesy name Jinglu, was from Yuanwu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Wanli 44.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事，歷員外郎、郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, and served successively as vice director and director.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of Justice as a principal clerk and rose through vice director to director.

sentences.zh: 恤刑陜西，釋疑獄百八十人。

translations.literal: On a mission to review punishments in Shaanxi, he released one hundred eighty persons from doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: While reviewing capital cases in Shaanxi he freed one hundred eighty prisoners whose guilt was uncertain.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，出為真定知府，遷井陘兵備副使，憂歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he went out as prefect of Zhending, was transferred to vice commissioner for military preparations at Jingxing, and returned home on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi he became prefect of Zhending, then vice commissioner for Jingxing military preparations, and returned home in mourning.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，起臨鞏兵備，改固原，再以憂歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was recalled to military preparations at Lingong, was transferred to Guyuan, and again returned on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 he was recalled to oversee defenses at Lingong, transferred to Guyuan, and again went home in mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起懷來兵備副使，移密雲。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete he was recalled as vice commissioner for military preparations at Huailai and was transferred to Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he resumed service as vice commissioner at Huailai and was moved to Miyun.

sentences.zh: 忤鎮守中官鄧希詔。

translations.literal: He offended the garrison eunuch Deng Xizhao.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with the garrison eunuch Deng Xizhao.

sentences.zh: 希詔摭他事劾之，下吏，削籍歸。

translations.literal: Xizhao seized on other matters to impeach him; he was handed over to the judicial authorities, struck from the rolls, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhao found other charges with which to impeach him; he was arrested, struck from the register, and sent home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 十五年詔舉邊才，用薦起故官，監通州軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year an edict called for men of frontier talent; on recommendation he was restored to his former office and supervised the army at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen an edict sought frontier talent; on recommendation he was restored to office and placed in charge of troops at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 勤王兵集都下，剽劫公行，割婦人首報功。

translations.literal: The troops coming to aid the throne gathered below the capital; plunder was openly practiced, and they cut off women's heads to report merit.
translations.idiomatic: Relief armies massed outside the capital, looting openly and even cutting off women's heads to claim battle honors.

sentences.zh: 師孔大怒，以其卒抵死。

translations.literal: Shikong was greatly angered and had his soldiers fight them to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Shikong flew into a rage and set his troops on them until they were killed.

sentences.zh: 明年，舉天下賢能方面官，鄭三俊薦師孔。

translations.literal: The following year, when men of talent for frontier posts were sought throughout the realm, Zheng Sanjun recommended Shikong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the court called for able frontier officials empire-wide, and Zheng Sanjun recommended Shikong.

sentences.zh: 六月，擢右僉都御史，代蔡官治巡撫陜西，調兵食，趣總督孫傳庭出關。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief, replaced Cai Guanzhi as grand coordinator of Shaanxi, gathered troops and provisions, and urged the governor-general Sun Chuanting to march out through the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi in place of Cai Guanzhi; he mustered men and grain and pressed governor-general Sun Chuanting to take the field beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，賊十三家七十二營降，師殆盡，惟李自成、張獻忠存。

translations.literal: At that time the thirteen bandit houses and seventy-two camps had for the most part surrendered and their forces were nearly exhausted; only Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong remained.
translations.idiomatic: By then the thirteen rebel houses and seventy-two camps had largely submitted and their armies were spent; only Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong still held out.

sentences.zh: 自成尤強，據襄陽。

translations.literal: Zicheng was especially strong and held Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng was the strongest of all and held Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 以河洛、荊襄四戰之地，關中其故鄉，士馬甲天下，據之可以霸，決策西向。

translations.literal: Because the lands of the Yellow and Luo rivers and of Jing-Xiang were battlegrounds on all sides, and Guanzhong was his homeland with soldiers and horses the finest under Heaven, holding them he could dominate; he resolved to march west.
translations.idiomatic: He judged that the Yellow-Luo and Jing-Xiang regions were perpetual battlegrounds, that Guanzhong was his homeland and its armies the finest in the empire, and that possession of them would make him master of the realm; he decided to strike west.

sentences.zh: 憚潼關天險，將自淅川龍車寨間道入陜西。

translations.literal: Fearing the natural barrier of Tong Pass, he planned to enter Shaanxi by a bypath from Xichuan through Longche Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Wary of the natural fortress at Tong Pass, he meant to slip into Shaanxi by a side route from Xichuan through Longche Stockade.

sentences.zh: 傳庭聞之，令師孔率四川、甘肅兵駐商、雒為掎角，而師孔趣戰。

translations.literal: Chuanting heard of this and ordered Shikong to lead the Sichuan and Gansu troops to garrison Shang and Luo in mutual support, but Shikong pressed for battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuanting learned of the plan he ordered Shikong to station Sichuan and Gansu troops at Shang and Luo in mutual support, but Shikong urged an immediate engagement.

sentences.zh: 無何，我師敗績於南陽，賊遂乘勝破潼關，大隊長驅，勢如破竹。

translations.literal: Before long our army was defeated at Nanyang; the bandits then took advantage of the victory to break Tong Pass, and their main force drove forward with momentum like splitting bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the imperial army was routed at Nanyang; the rebels pressed the advantage, smashed through Tong Pass, and swept forward in main force with irresistible momentum.

sentences.zh: 師孔整眾守西安，人或咎師孔趣師致敗也。

translations.literal: Shikong gathered his forces and defended Xi'an; some blamed Shikong's haste to give battle for the defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Shikong rallied his troops to hold Xi'an, though some blamed his eagerness to fight for the disaster.

sentences.zh: 賊至，守將王根子開門入之。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, the defending general Wang Genzi opened the gate and let them in.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, the garrison commander Wang Genzi opened the gates to them.

sentences.zh: 十月十一日，城陷，師孔投井死。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the tenth month the city fell; Shikong threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh of the tenth month the city fell and Shikong drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 同死者，按察使黃絅，長安知縣吳從義，秦府長史章尚絅，指揮崔爾達。

translations.literal: Those who died with him were the surveillance commissioner Huang Yin, the Chang'an magistrate Wu Congyi, the Qin princedom chief steward Zhang Shangjiong, and the commander Cui Erda.
translations.idiomatic: He was joined in death by surveillance commissioner Huang Yin, Chang'an magistrate Wu Congyi, Qin princedom chief steward Zhang Shangjiong, and commander Cui Erda.

sentences.zh: 炯，字季侯，光州人。

translations.literal: Yin, styled Jihou, was a native of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, courtesy name Jihou, was from Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in Tianqi 2.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，以淮海兵備副使憂歸。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen he returned home on mourning leave from his post as vice commissioner for military preparations on the Huai-Hai coast.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he went home in mourning from his post as Huai-Hai defense vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 流賊陷州城，絅方廬墓山中，子彜如死於賊，其妹亦被難。

translations.literal: When roving bandits took the prefectural city, Yin was dwelling by his father's tomb in the mountains; his son Yiru died at the hands of the bandits, and his younger sister also suffered in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits seized the prefectural seat, Yin was living in mourning seclusion in the hills; his son Yiru was killed by the rebels and his sister perished in the turmoil as well.

sentences.zh: 服除，起臨鞏兵備副使，調番兵，大破李自成潼關原。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete he was recalled as vice commissioner for military preparations at Lingong, mobilized tribal troops, and inflicted a great defeat on Li Zicheng at Tongguan Plain.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he resumed service at Lingong, raised tribal auxiliaries, and routed Li Zicheng on Tongguan Plain.

sentences.zh: 尋以右參政分守洮岷，擢陜西按察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made right administrative commissioner with divided defense of Tao and Min, and was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made right administrative commissioner for Tao and Min and then promoted to Shaanxi surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 自成勸之降，叱曰：「潼關之役，汝，我戮余也，今日肯降汝耶？

translations.literal: Zicheng urged him to surrender; he rebuked him, saying: "At the battle of Tong Pass you were my slaughtered remnant—would I surrender to you today?
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng urged him to submit; he shouted back, "At Tong Pass you were the butcher and I the butchered—would I bow to you now?

sentences.zh: 」妻王赴井，絅得間亦赴井，皆死。

translations.literal: " His wife Wang went into a well; Yin seized an opening and also went into a well—both died.
translations.idiomatic: " His wife Wang threw herself into a well; Yin found a moment and followed her—both died.

sentences.zh: 贈太常卿，謚忠烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the post of vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and given the posthumous title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with the posthumous title Zhonglie, "Loyal and Stern."

sentences.zh: 尚絅，會稽人。

translations.literal: Shangjiong was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjiong was from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 聞城陷，投印井中，冠服趨王府端禮門雉經。

translations.literal: Hearing that the city had fallen, he cast his seal into a well, donned cap and robes, and hurried to the princedom's Duanli Gate to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the city had fallen he threw his seal into a well, put on his official cap and robes, and hanged himself at the princedom's Duanli Gate.

sentences.zh: 贈按察司副使。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the post of vice surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made vice surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從義，山陰人。

translations.literal: Congyi was a native of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 兒時夢一人拊其背曰：「歲寒松柏，其在斯乎。

translations.literal: As a child he dreamed that a man clapped him on the back and said: "In cold years the pine and cypress—is it not here?
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he dreamed that someone clapped his shoulder and said, "When the year turns cold, the pine and cypress endure—is that not you?

sentences.zh: 」崇禎十三年成進士，之官，兵荒，從義練丁壯三百人殺賊。

translations.literal: " In the thirteenth year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi; on taking office, amid war and famine, Congyi drilled three hundred stalwart men and killed bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " He passed the metropolitan examination in Chongzhen 13; when he took up his post amid war and famine, he trained three hundred able-bodied men and fought the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊破秦，從義曰：「嗟乎，豈非天哉！

translations.literal: When the bandits broke Qin, Congyi said: "Alas, is this not Heaven's will!
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels overran Qin, Congyi said, "Alas—was this not foretold by Heaven!

sentences.zh: 吾唯昔夢是踐矣。

translations.literal: I have only to fulfill my former dream.
translations.idiomatic: I have only to fulfill the dream of my youth.

sentences.zh: 」遂投井死。

translations.literal: " He then threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 贈按察司僉事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the post of surveillance vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made surveillance vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 爾達，不知何許人，亦投井死之。

translations.literal: Erda, of unknown origin, also threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Erda, whose home is unknown, likewise drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 自是長安多義井。

translations.literal: From this time Chang'an had many wells of righteous death.
translations.idiomatic: After that Chang'an was dotted with wells remembered for righteous suicides.

sentences.zh: 賊遂執秦王存樞，處其宮署，置百官，稱王西安。

translations.literal: The bandits then seized the Qin prince Cunshu, occupied his palace offices, established the hundred officials, and proclaimed himself king at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized Prince Cunshu of Qin, took over the princely compound, set up a full bureaucracy, and proclaimed a kingdom at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 坐王府中，日執士大夫拷掠，索金錢，分兵四出攻抄。

translations.literal: Sitting in the princedom palace, day by day he seized scholar-officials for torture and extortion of gold and silver, and sent troops in all directions to attack and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: From the princely palace he had scholar-officials seized daily, tortured for gold and silver, and sent troops in every direction to raid and loot.

sentences.zh: 有小吏邱從周者，長不及三尺，乘醉罵自成曰：「若一小民無賴，妄踞王府，將僭偽號，而所為暴虐若此，何能久！

translations.literal: There was a minor clerk Qiu Congzhou, less than three chi in height, who when drunk cursed Zicheng, saying: "You, a petty rogue of the common people, have presumptuously occupied the princedom palace and are about to usurp a false title, yet your conduct is so cruel and violent—how can it last!
translations.idiomatic: A petty clerk named Qiu Congzhou, less than three feet tall, cursed Zicheng while drunk: "You base ruffian have seized the princely palace and mean to play at kingship, yet rule with such cruelty—how long can you last!

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，斫殺之。

translations.literal: " The bandits were enraged and hacked him to death.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels flew into a rage and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 而布政使平湖陸之祺及裏居吏部郎乾州宋企郊、提學僉事真寧鞏焴皆降賊，得寵用。

translations.literal: But the provincial administration commissioner Lu Zhiqi of Pinghu, the retired Ministry of Personnel director Song Qijiao of Qianzhou, and the education vice commissioner Gong Huang of Zhenning all surrendered to the bandits and were favored and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial administration commissioner Lu Zhiqi of Pinghu, retired Ministry of Personnel director Song Qijiao of Qianzhou, and education vice commissioner Gong Huang of Zhenning all submitted to the rebels and won favor.

sentences.zh: 先是，戶部尚書倪元璐奏曰：「天下諸藩，孰與秦、晉？

translations.literal: Earlier, the minister of revenue Ni Yuanlu memorialized, saying: "Among all the princedoms under Heaven, which compare with Qin and Jin?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Minister of Revenue Ni Yuanlu had memorialized: "Among all the imperial princedoms, which can match Qin and Jin?

sentences.zh: 秦晉山險，用武國也。

translations.literal: Qin and Jin lie among perilous mountains—they are states for the use of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Jin occupy rugged mountain country—they are martial domains by nature.

sentences.zh: 請諭二王，以剿賊保秦責秦王，以遏賊不入責晉王。

translations.literal: I ask that the two princes be instructed: charge the Qin prince with suppressing bandits to preserve Qin, and charge the Jin prince with blocking bandits from entering.
translations.idiomatic: Let the two princes be told that the Prince of Qin must suppress rebels to save Qin, and the Prince of Jin must keep rebels from entering Jin territory.

sentences.zh: 王能殺賊，假王以大將軍權；

translations.literal: If a prince can kill bandits, lend him the authority of a great general;
translations.idiomatic: If a prince can destroy the rebels, grant him the powers of a great general;

sentences.zh: 不能殺賊，悉輸王所有餉軍，與其賫盜。

translations.literal: if he cannot kill bandits, let him turn over all he possesses to supply the army, and share the fate of nourishing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: if he cannot, let him surrender all his wealth to feed the army rather than enrich the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊平，益封王各一子如親王，亦足以明報矣。

translations.literal: When bandits are pacified, enfeoff one son of each prince like a full imperial prince—that too would be sufficient clear recompense.
translations.idiomatic: When peace is restored, ennoble one son of each prince at the rank of a full imperial prince—that would be reward enough.

sentences.zh: 二王獨不鑒十一宗之禍乎？

translations.literal: Will the two princes alone fail to take warning from the calamity of the eleven clans?
translations.idiomatic: Will these two princes alone refuse to learn from the ruin of the eleven princedoms?

sentences.zh: 賢王忠而熟於計，必知所處矣。

translations.literal: Worthy princes who are loyal and skilled in planning will surely know how to conduct themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Princes who are loyal and shrewd will surely know what to do.

sentences.zh: 」書上，不報。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial went up unanswered.

sentences.zh: 至是，賊果破秦，悉為賊有焉。

translations.literal: At this time the bandits indeed broke Qin, and all fell into their possession.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rebels did break Qin, and the whole region fell into their hands.

sentences.zh: 林日瑞，字浴元，詔安人。

translations.literal: Lin Rirui, styled Yuyuan, was a native of Zhao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Rirui, courtesy name Yuyuan, was from Zhao'an.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Wanli 44.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，以江西右參政憂歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he returned home on mourning leave from his post as right administrative commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he went home in mourning from his post as right administrative commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起故官，分守湖廣。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete he was recalled to his former office and given divided defense of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he resumed his former rank with divided defense duties in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 屬縣鉛山界閩，妖人聚山中謀不軌，圍鉛山。

translations.literal: The subordinate county Qianshan bordered Fujian; sorcerers gathered in the mountains plotting sedition and besieged Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: The subordinate county of Qianshan bordered Fujian; cultists gathered in the hills to plot rebellion and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 日瑞擊敗之，搗其巢。

translations.literal: Rirui defeated them and destroyed their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Rirui routed them and destroyed their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 屢遷陜西左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to left and right provincial administration commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the left and right provincial administration commissions of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏，遷右僉都御史，代呂大器巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifteenth year he was transferred to right vice censor-in-chief and replaced Lü Daqi as grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year fifteen he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Gansu in place of Lü Daqi.

sentences.zh: 明年十一月，李自成屠慶陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the following year Li Zicheng massacred Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following eleventh month Li Zicheng sacked Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 其別將賀錦犯蘭州，蘭州人開城迎賊。

translations.literal: His lieutenant general He Jin attacked Lanzhou; the people of Lanzhou opened the city and welcomed the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His lieutenant He Jin struck at Lanzhou, and the townspeople opened the gates to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊遂渡河。

translations.literal: The bandits then crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then crossed the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 涼州、莊浪二衛降，即進逼甘州。

translations.literal: The two guards Liangzhou and Zhuanglang surrendered, and they at once pressed upon Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The guards of Liangzhou and Zhuanglang submitted, and the rebels advanced straight on Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 日瑞聞賊急，結西羌，嚴兵以待，而自率副將郭天吉等扼諸河干。

translations.literal: Rirui, hearing of the bandits' urgency, allied with the Western Qiang, arrayed troops strictly to await them, and himself led the vice generals Guo Tianji and others to block the river crossings.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the emergency, Rirui allied with the Western Qiang, marshaled his forces, and personally led vice generals including Guo Tianji to hold the river crossings.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊踏冰過，直抵甘州城下。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the bandits crossed on the ice and advanced straight to beneath the walls of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the rebels crossed on the ice and marched straight to the walls of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 日瑞入城，戰且守。

translations.literal: Rirui entered the city, fighting while defending.
translations.idiomatic: Rirui entered the city and fought on the walls.

sentences.zh: 大雪深丈許，樹盡介，角幹折，手足皸瘃，守者鹹怨。

translations.literal: Great snow lay more than a zhang deep; trees were all armored in ice, horn and trunk snapped, hands and feet chapped with frostbite—the defenders all murmured in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Snow lay more than ten feet deep; trees were encased in ice, branches snapped, and the defenders' hands and feet cracked with frost—all morale collapsed into bitter complaint.

sentences.zh: 賊乘夜坎雪而登，城陷，執日瑞。

translations.literal: The bandits took advantage of the night to pile snow into ramps and mount the walls; the city fell and Rirui was seized.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels piled snow into ramps by night and scaled the walls; the city fell and Rirui was taken.

sentences.zh: 誘以官，不從，磔於市。

translations.literal: They tempted him with office; he would not submit and was dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: They offered him office; he refused and was torn apart in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 初，日瑞撫甘肅，廷議以其不任也，遣楊汝經代之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Rirui governed Gansu, court discussion held that he was unequal to the task and Yang Rujing was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rirui first governed Gansu the court had judged him unequal to the post and sent Yang Rujing to replace him.

sentences.zh: 未至，日瑞遂及於難。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Rirui met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet arrived when Rirui met his end.

sentences.zh: 天吉及總兵官馬爌，撫標中軍哈維新、姚世儒，監紀同知藍臺，裏居總兵官羅俊傑、趙宦，並死之。

translations.literal: Tianji and the commander-in-chief Ma Huang, the grand coordinator's central army commanders Ha Weixin and Yao Shiru, the supervising secretary and subprefect Lan Tai, and the retired commanders Luo Junjie and Zhao Huan all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tianji, commander Ma Huang, grand-coordinator staff officers Ha Weixin and Yao Shiru, supervising secretary Lan Tai, and retired generals Luo Junjie and Zhao Huan all died with him.

sentences.zh: 賊殺居民四萬七千余人。

translations.literal: The bandits killed more than forty-seven thousand residents.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slaughtered more than forty-seven thousand civilians.

sentences.zh: 三邊既陷，列城望風降，惟西寧衛固守不下。

translations.literal: Once the Three Frontiers had fallen, successive cities surrendered at the mere sight of the enemy; only Xining Guard held firm and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: With the Three Frontiers lost, city after city submitted at the rebels' approach; only Xining Guard held out.

sentences.zh: 賊無後顧，乃長驅而東。

translations.literal: With no rear to worry about, they then drove east at full speed.
translations.idiomatic: Free of any threat behind them, they marched east at full speed.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈日瑞兵部尚書，臺太仆寺少卿，皆賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu, Rirui was posthumously granted minister of war, and Tai vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; both were granted sacrificial rites and burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Rirui was posthumously made minister of war and Lan Tai vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; both were granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 蔡懋德，字維立，昆山人。

translations.literal: Cai Maode, styled Weili, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Maode, courtesy name Weili, was from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 少慕王守仁為人，著《管見》，宗良知之說。

translations.literal: In youth he admired Wang Shouren as a man; he wrote Guanjian and followed Liangzhi's teachings.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he admired Wang Shouren and wrote Guanjian, taking Liangzhi's philosophy as his guide.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷四十七年進士，授杭州推官。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Wanli he became a jinshi and was appointed investigating censor of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 47 and was appointed investigating censor of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 天啟間，行取入都。

translations.literal: During Tianqi he was selected by special promotion and entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianqi he was selected for capital service by special promotion.

sentences.zh: 同鄉顧秉謙柄國，懋德不與通，秉謙怒，以故不得顯擢。

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Gu Bingqian held power in the state; Maode would not associate with him, Bingqian was angered, and for this reason he did not receive prominent advancement.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Gu Bingqian dominated the government; Maode refused all contact, Gu took offense, and Maode was passed over for high promotion.

sentences.zh: 授禮部儀制主事，進祠祭員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites for ceremonial regulations, and advanced to vice director for ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of Rites as principal clerk for ceremonial regulations and rose to vice director for ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尚書率諸司往謁魏忠賢祠，懋德托疾不赴。

translations.literal: The minister led the various bureaus to pay homage at the shrine of Wei Zhongxian; Maode pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the minister led the bureaus to worship at Wei Zhongxian's shrine, Maode pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，出為江西提學副使，好以守仁《拔本塞源論》教諸生，大抵釋氏之緒論。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he went out as education vice commissioner of Jiangxi; he liked to teach students with Shouren's Baben Siyuan Lun, which for the most part were Buddhist-style discourses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he became Jiangxi education vice commissioner and taught students from Shouren's Baben Siyuan Lun—discourses that were largely Buddhist in tone.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江右參政，分守嘉興、湖州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right administrative commissioner of Zhejiang with divided defense of Jiaxing and Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right administrative commissioner of Zhejiang with defense duties at Jiaxing and Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 劇盜屠阿醜有眾千余，出沒太湖。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Tu A'chou had a following of more than a thousand and ranged over Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit chieftain Tu A'chou commanded more than a thousand men and raided around Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 懋德曰：「此可計擒也。

translations.literal: Maode said: "This one can be taken by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Maode said, "This fellow can be taken by a ruse.

sentences.zh: 」悉召瀕湖豪家，把其罪，簡壯士與同發，遂擒阿醜。

translations.literal: " He summoned all the powerful families along the lake, seized on their crimes, selected stalwart men to set out with him, and thus captured A'chou.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned the powerful families along the lake, held their crimes over them, picked stalwart men from among them, and captured A'chou.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「懋德知兵。

translations.literal: All said: "Maode understands warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone said, "Maode understands war.

sentences.zh: 」內艱，服除，起井陘兵備。

translations.literal: " On mourning for his mother, when mourning was complete he was recalled to military preparations at Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: " After mourning his mother he resumed service as Jingxing defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旱，懋德禱，即雨。

translations.literal: During drought Maode prayed, and rain came at once.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought Maode prayed and rain fell at once.

sentences.zh: 他鄉爭迎以禱，又輒雨。

translations.literal: Other districts competed to welcome him to pray, and again rain came each time.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring districts competed to bring him in to pray, and rain followed each time.

sentences.zh: 調寧遠，以守松山及修臺堡功，數敘賚。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Ningyuan; for his achievements in defending Songshan and repairing platform forts, rewards were repeatedly entered on the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Ningyuan, where his defense of Songshan and repair of platform forts won him repeated rewards.

sentences.zh: 會災異求言，懋德上《省過》、《治平》二疏，規切君相，一時鹹笑為迂。

translations.literal: When omens and disasters prompted a call for memorials, Maode submitted two memorials, Sheng Guo and Zhi Ping, admonishing ruler and chief minister; for a time all laughed at him as pedantic.
translations.idiomatic: When omens prompted a call for frank counsel, Maode submitted his Sheng Guo and Zhi Ping memorials, rebuking emperor and chief minister alike; contemporaries dismissed him as hopelessly earnest.

sentences.zh: 懋德好釋氏，律身如苦行頭陀。

translations.literal: Maode favored Buddhism and disciplined his person like an ascetic dhuta.
translations.idiomatic: Maode was devoted to Buddhism and disciplined himself like an ascetic monk.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌謂其清修弱質，不宜處邊地，改濟南道。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang said that his pure cultivation and weak constitution were unsuited to frontier posts, and transferred him to the Jinan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang judged his ascetic habits and slight frame unsuited to the frontier and moved him to the Jinan circuit.

sentences.zh: 濟南新殘破，大吏多缺人，懋德攝兩司及三道印。

translations.literal: Jinan had newly been ravaged; high officials were mostly short of men, and Maode concurrently held the seals of the two commissions and the three circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan had just been devastated and senior posts were vacant; Maode held the seals of both commissions and all three circuits at once.

sentences.zh: 遷山東按察使、河南右布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Shandong and right provincial administration commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He became Shandong surveillance commissioner and then right provincial administration commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 田荒谷貴，民苦催科，賊復以先服不輸租相煽誘。

translations.literal: Fields lay waste and grain was dear; the people suffered under tax collection, and bandits further incited them with the claim that those who had submitted earlier need not pay rent.
translations.idiomatic: Fields lay fallow and grain was dear; the people groaned under tax levies, and rebels stirred them up with promises that those who had once submitted need pay no rent.

sentences.zh: 懋德亟檄州縣停征，上疏自劾，詔鐫七級視事。

translations.literal: Maode urgently ordered the prefectures and counties to halt collection, memorialized impeaching himself, and an edict reduced his rank by seven grades while he continued in office.
translations.idiomatic: Maode urgently ordered the districts to halt collection, memorialized impeaching himself, and was ordered to continue in office after a seven-grade demotion.

sentences.zh: 十四年冬，擢右僉都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year fourteen he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 召對，賜酒饌、銀幣。

translations.literal: He was summoned for audience, and granted wine, food, silver, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, he was given wine, food, silver, and silk.

sentences.zh: 明年春，抵任，討平大盜王冕。

translations.literal: The next spring he reached his post and suppressed the great bandit Wang Mian.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he took up his post and put down the bandit chieftain Wang Mian.

sentences.zh: 十月，統兵入衛京師，詔扼守龍泉、固關二關。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he led troops to guard the capital; an edict ordered him to hold the two passes of Longquan and Guguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he marched troops to defend the capital and was ordered to hold the Longquan and Guguan passes.

sentences.zh: 李自成已陷河南，懋德禦之河上。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng had already taken Henan, and Maode defended against him on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had already overrun Henan, and Maode held the line along the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，自成破潼關，據西安，盡有三秦。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year Zicheng broke through Tongguan, seized Xi'an, and held all the Three Qins.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year sixteen Zicheng broke through Tongguan, took Xi'an, and controlled all of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，懋德師次平陽，遣副將陳尚智扼守河津。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Maode's army halted at Pingyang and sent the deputy commander Chen Shangzhi to hold Hejin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Maode encamped at Pingyang and sent deputy commander Chen Shangzhi to hold Hejin.

sentences.zh: 山西、京師右背、蒲州北抵保德，悉鄰賊，依黃河為險。

translations.literal: Shanxi, the right flank of the capital, and the region north from Puzhou to Baode all bordered the bandits and relied on the Yellow River as a barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi, the capital's right flank, and the country from Puzhou north to Baode all bordered rebel territory and looked to the Yellow River for protection.

sentences.zh: 然窮冬冰合，賊騎得長驅。

translations.literal: Yet in the depths of winter the ice joined, and the bandit cavalry could drive straight through.
translations.idiomatic: But in deep winter the river froze solid, and rebel horsemen could ride straight across.

sentences.zh: 懋德連章告急，請禁旅及保定、宣府、大同兵疾赴河干合拒。

translations.literal: Maode repeatedly memorialized in emergency, requesting the capital garrison and troops from Baoding, Xuanfu, and Datong to hurry to the riverbank and block together.
translations.idiomatic: Maode sent urgent memorial after urgent memorial asking the capital garrison and forces from Baoding, Xuanfu, and Datong to rush to the river and join in blocking the enemy.

sentences.zh: 中朝益積憂山西，言防河者甚眾，然無兵可援。

translations.literal: The court grew ever more anxious about Shanxi; many spoke of defending the river, yet no troops could be sent to aid.
translations.idiomatic: The court grew increasingly alarmed for Shanxi; many officials urged river defense, but no reinforcements could be spared.

sentences.zh: 懋德以疲卒三千，當百萬狂寇。

translations.literal: Maode with three thousand exhausted soldiers faced a million reckless bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Maode stood with three thousand worn-out troops against a horde said to number a million.

sentences.zh: 時太原洶洶，晉王手教趣懋德還省。

translations.literal: At the time Taiyuan was in turmoil; the Prince of Jin personally wrote urging Maode to return to the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan was in uproar, and the Prince of Jin sent a personal letter urging Maode back to the provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 十八日，懋德去平陽。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day Maode left Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth Maode withdrew from Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 二十日，賊抵河津，自船窩東渡，尚智走還平陽。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day the bandits reached Hejin, crossed east from Chuanwo by boat, and Shangzhi fled back to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth the rebels reached Hejin, crossed east from Chuanwo by boat, and Shangzhi fled back to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 二十二日，賊攻平陽，拔之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day the bandits attacked Pingyang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second the rebels stormed Pingyang and captured it.

sentences.zh: 尚智奔入泥源山中。

translations.literal: Shangzhi fled into the Niyuan mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi fled into the mountains at Niyuan.

sentences.zh: 二十八日，懋德還太原。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day Maode returned to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth Maode returned to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，自成稱王於西安。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Zicheng proclaimed himself king at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month Zicheng declared himself king at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 賊既渡河，轉掠河東，列城皆陷。

translations.literal: Once the bandits had crossed the river, they turned to plunder the east bank and every walled city fell.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river the rebels turned to ravage the east bank, and walled city after walled city fell.

sentences.zh: 於是山西巡按御史汪宗友上言曰：「晉河二千里，平陽居其半。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Shanxi touring censor Wang Zongyou memorialized, saying: "The rivers of Shanxi stretch two thousand li; Pingyang lies at their midpoint.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shanxi touring censor Wang Zongyou memorialized, saying, "Shanxi's rivers run two thousand li, and Pingyang stands at their center.

sentences.zh: 撫臣懋德不待春融冰泮，遽爾平陽返旆，賊即於明日報渡矣。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Maode, without waiting for the spring thaw and ice melt, abruptly withdrew his banners from Pingyang, and the very next day came report that the bandits had crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Maode did not wait for the spring thaw but abruptly withdrew from Pingyang, and the very next day came word that the rebels had crossed.

sentences.zh: 隨行馬步千人，即時倍道西向，召集陳尚智叛卒，移檄各路防兵援剿，乃不發一兵。

translations.literal: The thousand horse and foot who accompanied him should at once have marched double-time westward, gathered Chen Shangzhi's rebel soldiers, and issued proclamations to defensive forces on every route to reinforce and suppress the enemy—yet not one soldier was sent.
translations.idiomatic: The thousand horse and foot who had gone with him should have marched at forced speed westward at once, rallied Chen Shangzhi's scattered troops, and called on every defensive garrison to reinforce and strike—yet not one soldier was dispatched.

sentences.zh: 歲終至省，臣言宜提一旅，星馳而前，張疑聲討，尚冀桑榆之收，無如不聽何。

translations.literal: By year's end he reached the provincial capital; your subject said he should lead one brigade, ride ahead at star speed, raise a feinting alarm and attack, and one might still hope for a late recovery—but what could be done when he would not listen?
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the provincial capital at year's end, your subject urged him to lead a single detachment and ride ahead at forced march to threaten the enemy with a feint, still hoping for a late recovery—but what could be done when he would not listen?

sentences.zh: 賊日遣偽官，匝月，余郡皆失，是誰之過歟！

translations.literal: The bandits daily sent pretended officials; within a full month the remaining prefectures were all lost—whose fault is this!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent their pretended officials day after day, and within a month the remaining prefectures were all lost. Whose fault is this!

sentences.zh: 」有詔奪官候勘，以郭景昌代之。

translations.literal: " An edict stripped him of office pending investigation, and Guo Jingchang was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict stripped Maode of office pending investigation and appointed Guo Jingchang to replace him.

sentences.zh: 二十三日，尚智叛降於賊。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day Shangzhi rebelled and surrendered to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third Shangzhi defected and surrendered to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 於是懋德誓師於太原，布政使趙建極，監司毛文炳、藺剛中、畢拱辰，太原知府孫康周，署陽曲縣事長史範誌泰等官吏軍民鹹在。

translations.literal: Thereupon Maode rallied the army at Taiyuan; Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhao Jianji, the surveillance commissioners Mao Wenbing, Lin Gangzhong, and Bi Gongchen, Taiyuan prefect Sun Kangzhou, Chief Clerk Fan Zhita acting as magistrate of Yangqu County, and other officials, soldiers, and civilians were all present.
translations.idiomatic: Maode then rallied the troops at Taiyuan. Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhao Jianji, surveillance commissioners Mao Wenbing, Lin Gangzhong, and Bi Gongchen, Taiyuan prefect Sun Kangzhou, Chief Clerk Fan Zhita acting as magistrate of Yangqu, and the rest of the officials, soldiers, and people were all there.

sentences.zh: 懋德哭，眾皆哭。

translations.literal: Maode wept, and all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Maode wept, and everyone wept with him.

sentences.zh: 罷官命適至，或請出城候代。

translations.literal: The order removing him from office happened to arrive, and some asked that he leave the city to await his replacement.
translations.idiomatic: The order stripping him of office arrived just then, and some urged him to leave the city and await his successor.

sentences.zh: 懋德不可，曰：「吾已辦一死矣，景昌即至，吾亦與俱死。

translations.literal: Maode would not agree and said: "I have already prepared myself for death; when Jingchang arrives, I too shall die with him.
translations.idiomatic: Maode refused, saying, "I have already resolved to die. When Jingchang arrives, I shall die with him as well.

sentences.zh: 」調陽和兵三千協守東門。

translations.literal: " He assigned three thousand Yanghe troops to help defend the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: " He assigned three thousand Yanghe troops to help hold the east gate.

sentences.zh: 剛中慮其內應，移之南關之外。

translations.literal: Gangzhong, fearing they would serve as inside collaborators, moved them outside the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong, fearing they would collude from within, posted them outside the south gate.

sentences.zh: 遣部將張雄分守新南門，召中軍副總兵應時盛入參謀議。

translations.literal: He sent the division commander Zhang Xiong to help defend the new south gate separately and summoned the central-army deputy commander Ying Shisheng in to join the council of strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He sent division commander Zhang Xiong to hold the new south gate and summoned deputy commander Ying Shisheng of the central army to join the war council.

sentences.zh: 懋德等登城。

translations.literal: Maode and the others mounted the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Maode and the others went up on the walls.

sentences.zh: 二月五日，賊至城下。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the second month the bandits reached the foot of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth of the second month the rebels reached the city walls.

sentences.zh: 遣部將牛勇、朱孔訓、王永魁出戰，死之。

translations.literal: He sent the division commanders Niu Yong, Zhu Kongxun, and Wang Yongkui out to fight, and they died.
translations.idiomatic: He sent division commanders Niu Yong, Zhu Kongxun, and Wang Yongkui out to fight, and all three were killed.

sentences.zh: 明日，自成具鹵簿，督眾攻城，陽和兵叛降賊。

translations.literal: The next day Zicheng brought out the full imperial regalia, supervised the masses in storming the wall, and the Yanghe troops rebelled and surrendered to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zicheng appeared with full imperial regalia, directed the assault on the walls, and the Yanghe troops defected to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 又明日，晝晦，懋德草遺表。

translations.literal: Again the next day the daylight darkened, and Maode drafted his death memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The day after that daylight turned dark, and Maode drafted his final memorial.

sentences.zh: 須臾大風起，拔木揚砂。

translations.literal: In a moment a great wind rose, uprooting trees and whirling sand.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a fierce wind rose, uprooting trees and hurling sand through the air.

sentences.zh: 調張雄守大南門，雄已縋城出降，語其黨曰：「城東南角樓，火器火藥皆在，我下即焚樓。

translations.literal: Maode reassigned Zhang Xiong to defend the great south gate, but Xiong had already lowered himself by rope from the wall and surrendered; he told his fellows: "At the southeast corner tower are stored all the firearms and gunpowder; once I descend I shall burn the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Maode reassigned Zhang Xiong to the great south gate, but Xiong had already lowered himself from the wall by rope and surrendered, telling his comrades, "All the firearms and gunpowder are in the southeast corner tower. Once I come down I shall burn it.

sentences.zh: 」夜中火起，風轉烈，守者皆散。

translations.literal: " At night fire broke out; the wind grew fiercer still, and the defenders all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: " That night fire broke out. The wind grew fiercer still, and the defenders fled in every direction.

sentences.zh: 賊登城，懋德北面再拜，出遺表付友人賈士璋間道達京師，語人曰：「吾學道有年，已勘了死生，今日吾致命時也。

translations.literal: The bandits mounted the wall; Maode bowed twice facing north, entrusted his death memorial to his friend Jia Shizhang to reach the capital by a hidden route, and said to those around him: "I have studied the Way for many years and have already resolved the question of life and death; today is the day I give my life.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels scaled the walls. Maode bowed twice toward the north, gave his death memorial to his friend Jia Shizhang to carry to the capital by a secret route, and told those around him, "I have studied the Way for many years and have already settled the question of life and death. Today is the day I give my life.

sentences.zh: 」即自剄，麾下持之。

translations.literal: " At once he cut his own throat; his attendants held him up.
translations.idiomatic: " At once he cut his own throat, and his attendants held him up.

sentences.zh: 時盛請下城巷戰，顧懋德曰：「上馬。

translations.literal: Shisheng asked to descend and fight in the lanes, turned to Maode, and said: "Mount your horse.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng asked to go down and fight in the streets, turned to Maode, and said, "Mount up.

sentences.zh: 」懋德上馬，時盛持矛突殺賊數十人。

translations.literal: " Maode mounted his horse; Shisheng, spear in hand, charged and killed dozens of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " Maode mounted, and Shisheng, spear in hand, charged through and killed dozens of rebels.

sentences.zh: 至炭市口，賊騎充斥，時盛呼曰：「出西門。

translations.literal: Reaching Tanishikou, bandit cavalry filled the streets; Shisheng shouted: "Out the west gate!
translations.idiomatic: At Tanishikou rebel horsemen filled the streets. Shisheng shouted, "Out the west gate!

sentences.zh: 」懋德遽下馬曰：「我當死封疆，諸君自去。

translations.literal: " Maode abruptly dismounted and said: "I am bound to die defending this territory; the rest of you go on your way.
translations.idiomatic: " Maode dismounted at once and said, "I am bound to die defending this territory. The rest of you go on.

sentences.zh: 」眾復擁懋德上馬，至水西門。

translations.literal: " The crowd again pressed Maode onto his horse, and they reached the west water gate.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd pressed Maode back onto his horse again and they reached the west water gate.

sentences.zh: 懋德叱曰：「諸君欲陷我不忠耶！

translations.literal: Maode rebuked them, saying: "Do you wish to make me disloyal!
translations.idiomatic: Maode rebuked them, saying, "Do you mean to make a traitor of me!

sentences.zh: 」復下馬，據地坐。

translations.literal: " He dismounted again and sat on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: " He dismounted again and sat down on the ground.

sentences.zh: 時盛已出城，殺妻子，還顧不見，復斫門入，語懋德曰：「請與公俱死。

translations.literal: Shisheng had already left the city, killed his wife and children, looked back and not seeing Maode, hacked through the gate again and entered, and said to Maode: "I beg to die with you, sir.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng had already left the city, killed his wife and children, looked back and not seeing Maode, hacked his way back through the gate, and said to him, "I ask to die with you, sir.

sentences.zh: 」遂偕至三立祠。

translations.literal: " Together they went to the Sanli Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: " Together they went to the Sanli Shrine.

sentences.zh: 懋德就縊未絕，時盛釋甲加其肩，乃絕。

translations.literal: Maode had hanged himself but was not yet dead; Shisheng removed his armor and placed it on Maode's shoulders, and then he died.
translations.idiomatic: Maode had hanged himself but was not yet dead. Shisheng removed his armor and laid it on Maode's shoulders, and then Maode died.

sentences.zh: 時盛取弓弦自經。

translations.literal: Shisheng took a bowstring and strangled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng took a bowstring and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 建極危坐公堂，賊擁之見自成，不屈，將斬之。

translations.literal: Jianji sat upright in the public hall; the bandits forced him before Zicheng; he would not submit, and they were about to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji sat upright in the hall of government. The rebels dragged him before Zicheng; he refused to submit, and they were about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 下階呼萬歲者再，曰：「臣失守封疆，死有余罪。

translations.literal: Descending the steps he cried "Long live!" twice and said: "Your subject failed to hold the territory, and death would not expiate the guilt.
translations.idiomatic: As he came down the steps he cried "Long live!" twice and said, "Your subject failed to hold the territory, and even death would not expiate the guilt.

sentences.zh: 」自成以為呼己也，曳還。

translations.literal: " Zicheng thought he was hailing him and had him dragged back.
translations.idiomatic: " Zicheng thought Jianji was hailing him and had him dragged back.

sentences.zh: 建極瞋目曰：「我呼大明皇帝，寧呼賊耶！

translations.literal: Jianji glared and said: "I was calling on the Great Ming emperor—would I call on a bandit!
translations.idiomatic: Jianji glared and said, "I was calling on the Great Ming emperor. Would I call on a bandit!

sentences.zh: 」立射殺之。

translations.literal: " He was immediately shot dead.
translations.idiomatic: " He was shot dead on the spot.

sentences.zh: 時自成執晉王，據王宮雲。

translations.literal: At the time Zicheng held the Prince of Jin and occupied the princely palace.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zicheng held the Prince of Jin and occupied the princely palace.

sentences.zh: 文炳被殺，妻趙、妾李亦投井死，子兆夢甫數歲，賊掠去。

translations.literal: Wenbing was killed; his wife Zhao and concubine Li also threw themselves into a well and died; his son Zhaomeng was only a few years old and was carried off by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing was killed. His wife Zhao and concubine Li threw themselves into a well and died. His son Zhaomeng, only a few years old, was carried off by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 士民以其忠臣子也，贖而歸之。

translations.literal: The gentry and common people, because he was the son of a loyal minister, ransomed him and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was the son of a loyal minister, the townspeople ransomed him and brought him home.

sentences.zh: 欲降剛中，不從，殺之。

translations.literal: They wished to make Gangzhong submit; he would not obey, and they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to force Gangzhong to submit; he refused, and they killed him.

sentences.zh: 首即墮，復躍起丈余，賊皆辟易。

translations.literal: His head fell at once, yet he leaped up again more than a zhang; the bandits all fell back in fear.
translations.idiomatic: His head fell at once, yet his body leaped up more than ten feet; the rebels all shrank back in terror.

sentences.zh: 賊適得新刀，拱辰睨之。

translations.literal: The bandits had just obtained a new blade, and Gongchen glanced sidelong at it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had just acquired a new blade, and Gongchen glanced at it.

sentences.zh: 問：「何睨！

translations.literal: They asked: "Why the sidelong look!
translations.idiomatic: They asked, "Why the sidelong look!

sentences.zh: 」曰：「欲得此斫頭耳。

translations.literal: " He said: "I only wanted this blade to cut off your head.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "I only wanted that blade to cut off your head.

sentences.zh: 」遂取斬之。

translations.literal: " So they took it and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " So they took the blade and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 康周巷戰死，誌泰不食死。

translations.literal: Kangzhou died fighting in the lanes; Zhita died by refusing food.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzhou died fighting in the streets, and Zhita starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 自懋德而下，太原死事凡四十有六人，賊皆屍之城上。

translations.literal: From Maode downward, those who died for the cause at Taiyuan numbered forty-six in all; the bandits piled their corpses on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: From Maode on down, forty-six people died defending Taiyuan, and the rebels piled their bodies on the walls.

sentences.zh: 自成恨懋德之不降也，驗其屍，以刃斷頸而去。

translations.literal: Zicheng hated Maode for not submitting; he inspected the corpse, severed the neck with a blade, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng hated Maode for refusing to submit; he inspected the body, hacked through the neck with a blade, and left.

sentences.zh: 福王時，以懋德不守河為失策，乃謚忠襄，賜祭葬而不予贈蔭，余賜恤有差。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, because Maode had failed to hold the river was judged a strategic error; he was given the posthumous name Zhongxiang, granted sacrificial rites and burial but not posthumous honors or benefits for descendants, while the others received graded condolence awards.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Maode's failure to hold the river was judged a strategic mistake; he was given the posthumous name Zhongxiang and granted sacrificial rites and burial, but not posthumous honors or benefits for his descendants, while the others received graded awards of condolence.

sentences.zh: 間考四十六人，行事多缺，姓名不傳，莫得而次雲。

translations.literal: On examining the forty-six in detail, the records of their deeds were mostly incomplete and their names untransmitted, so they could not be ranked in order.
translations.idiomatic: On closer examination of the forty-six, most of their deeds were poorly recorded and their names were not preserved, so they cannot be listed in order.

sentences.zh: 建極，河南永寧人。

translations.literal: Jianji was a native of Yongning in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji was from Yongning in Henan.

sentences.zh: 賊掠永寧時，建極五子皆死，後生三子又夭，至是趙氏一門竟絕。

translations.literal: When the bandits plundered Yongning, all five of Jianji's sons died; later three more sons were born and also died young; by this time the Zhao clan was extinguished to the last.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits ravaged Yongning, all five of Jianji's sons died. Three more sons born later also died young, and by then the Zhao line was extinguished altogether.

sentences.zh: 文炳，字夢石，鄭州人。

translations.literal: Wenbing, styled Mengshi, was a native of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing, courtesy name Mengshi, was from Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 以吏科給事中出為山西兵備副使。

translations.literal: From supervising secretary in the Office of Personnel he went out as vice commissioner for military preparations in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Office of Personnel as a supervising secretary to become Shanxi vice commissioner for military preparations.

sentences.zh: 為給事時，楊嗣昌督師，議調民兵討賊。

translations.literal: When he was a supervising secretary, Yang Sichang was grand coordinator of armies and proposed mobilizing militia to suppress the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as supervising secretary, he served under Yang Sichang as grand coordinator and debated mobilizing militia to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 文炳言：「民兵可守不可調，不若官軍乘馬便殺賊。

translations.literal: Wenbing said: "Militia can defend but cannot be mobilized; better to have regular troops on horseback to kill bandits readily.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing said, "Militia can hold ground but should not be mobilized. Regular cavalry are better suited to killing bandits.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「當大計，主計者喜奔競，抑廉靜，宜令官得互糾不公者。

translations.literal: " He also said: "At the grand evaluation, those in charge of assessment favor frantic rivalry and suppress the quiet and upright; officials should be allowed to impeach one another for injustice.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "At the grand evaluation those who control the assessments favor frantic self-promotion and suppress the quiet and upright. Officials should be allowed to impeach one another for injustice.

sentences.zh: 」帝皆納其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted all his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 剛中，字坦生，陵縣人。

translations.literal: Gangzhong, styled Tansheng, was a native of Ling County.
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong, courtesy name Tansheng, was from Ling County.

sentences.zh: 為南京給事中，奏保護留都六事，又陳漕事救弊之要。

translations.literal: As a Nanjing supervising secretary he memorialized six measures to protect the southern capital and also set forth the essentials for remedying abuses in grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: As a Nanjing supervising secretary he memorialized six measures to protect the southern capital and laid out the essentials for reforming abuses in the grain transport system.

sentences.zh: 山東饑，疏言：「民死而丁存，田荒而賦在，安得不為盜！

translations.literal: When Shandong suffered famine he memorialized, saying: "The people are dead but corvée obligations remain; fields lie waste but taxes remain—how can they not turn to banditry!
translations.idiomatic: During famine in Shandong he memorialized, saying, "The people are dead but corvée obligations remain; fields lie waste but taxes remain. How can they not turn to banditry!

sentences.zh: 宜清戶口並裏甲。

translations.literal: Household registers and village registers should be cleared and consolidated.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers and village registers should be cleared and consolidated.

sentences.zh: 」皆切時病。

translations.literal: " All struck at the ailments of the times.
translations.idiomatic: " All struck at the ailments of the times.

sentences.zh: 遷山西副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 拱辰，字星伯，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Gongchen, styled Xingbo, was a native of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchen, courtesy name Xingbo, was from Ye County.

sentences.zh: 知朝邑、鹽城二縣，數遷數貶。
