translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Chaoyi and Yancheng counties and was repeatedly promoted and repeatedly demoted.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Chaoyi and Yancheng and was promoted and demoted again and again.

sentences.zh: 歷淮徐兵備僉事，督漕侍郎史可法謂其不任，移之冀寧。

translations.literal: He served as assistant commissioner for military preparations on the Huai-Xu circuit; Grand Secretary of Grain Transport Shi Kefa judged him unfit and transferred him to Jining.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant commissioner for military preparations on the Huai-Xu circuit, but Transport Commissioner Shi Kefa judged him unfit and moved him to Jining.

sentences.zh: 建極、文炳、剛中、拱辰由進士。

translations.literal: Jianji, Wenbing, Gangzhong, and Gongchen entered by the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji, Wenbing, Gangzhong, and Gongchen all entered service as jinshi graduates.

sentences.zh: 康周，字晉侯，安丘人，由鄉舉。

translations.literal: Kangzhou, styled Jinhou, was a native of Anqiu and entered by the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzhou, courtesy name Jinhou, was from Anqiu and entered by the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 時盛，遼陽諸生。

translations.literal: Shisheng was a licentiate of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng was a licentiate from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 為懋德所知，拔隸幕下，至都督僉事。

translations.literal: Known to Maode, he was selected to serve under his staff and rose to vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized by Maode, he was brought onto his staff and rose to vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 誌泰，虞城人。

translations.literal: Zhita was a native of Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhita was from Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 余莫考。

translations.literal: The rest I cannot verify.
translations.idiomatic: The rest I have been unable to trace.

sentences.zh: 太原既破，賊移檄遠近，所至郡縣望風結寨以拒官兵。

translations.literal: Once Taiyuan had fallen, the bandits issued proclamations far and near; wherever they went the prefectures and counties, seeing the wind, fortified camps to resist government troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiyuan fell the rebels issued proclamations far and wide, and wherever they went local prefectures and counties fortified camps at the first rumor to resist government troops.

sentences.zh: 而其仗義死難，陷胸斷脰而甘心者，則有若安邑知縣房之屏，宛平人，起家鄉舉。

translations.literal: Yet among those who upheld righteousness, died in calamity, and willingly suffered pierced breasts and severed necks, there was such a one as Anyi magistrate Fang Zhiping, a native of Wanping who began his career through the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among those who upheld righteousness and willingly met death—even pierced breasts and severed necks—was Anyi magistrate Fang Zhiping of Wanping, who had begun his career through the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 城陷，北向拜天子，入署拜其母，命妻子各自盡，遂投井，賊曳出斬之。

translations.literal: When the city fell he bowed north toward the Son of Heaven, entered the yamen and bowed to his mother, ordered his wife and children each to take their own lives, then threw himself into a well; the bandits dragged him out and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he bowed toward the emperor in the north, went to the yamen and bowed to his mother, ordered his wife and children to take their own lives, then threw himself into a well. The rebels dragged him out and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 忻州知州楊家龍，字惕若，曲陽人。

translations.literal: Xinzhou prefect Yang Jialong, styled Tiruo, was a native of Quyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhou prefect Yang Jialong, courtesy name Tiruo, was from Quyang.

sentences.zh: 為寧鄉知縣，凡七年，流亡復其業。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Ningxiang for seven years in all and restored refugees to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He had served seven years as magistrate of Ningxiang and restored refugees to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 遷忻，賊即至，曰：「此城必不守，我出，爾民可全也。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xin; the bandits arrived at once. He said: "This city cannot be held. If I go out, your people may be spared.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to Xinzhou, the rebels arrived immediately. He said, "This city cannot be held. If I go out, your people may be spared.

sentences.zh: 」出城罵賊而死。

translations.literal: " He went out of the city, cursed the bandits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He went out of the city, cursed the rebels, and died.

sentences.zh: 州人祠祀之。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture enshrined and worshipped him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture built a shrine to him and offered sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 代州參將閻夢夔，鹿邑人，汾州知州侯君昭，皆城亡與亡。

translations.literal: Yan Mengkui, assistant commander of Daizhou, a native of Luyi, and Hou Junzhao, prefect of Fenzhou, both perished when their cities fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Mengkui, assistant commander at Daizhou, from Luyi, and Hou Junzhao, prefect of Fenzhou, both died when their cities fell.

sentences.zh: 汾陽知縣劉必達袖出罵賊文，賊誦而殺之。

translations.literal: Liu Bida, magistrate of Fenyang, pulled from his sleeve a written denunciation of the bandits; the bandits read it aloud and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bida, magistrate of Fenyang, drew from his sleeve a written tirade against the rebels; they read it aloud and killed him.

sentences.zh: 其義勇範奇芳，刺殺一偽都尉而自剄。

translations.literal: One valiant civilian, Fan Qifang, stabbed and killed a false colonel and then cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: A local volunteer, Fan Qifang, stabbed and killed a rebel colonel and then cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 寧武兵備副使王孕懋，字有懷，由太原知府遷。

translations.literal: Wang Yunmao, deputy commissioner for military preparations at Ningwu, styled Youhuai, was transferred from the post of prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yunmao, deputy commissioner for military preparations at Ningwu, courtesy name Youhuai, had been transferred from the prefecture of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 自成既陷太原，遣使說降，孕懋斬之，與總兵官周遇吉共守，城陷自殺，妻楊投井殉之。

translations.literal: After Zicheng had taken Taiyuan, he sent emissaries to urge surrender; Yunmao beheaded them and, together with the regional commander Zhou Yuji, jointly defended the city. When the city fell he killed himself, and his wife Yang threw herself into a well in martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Zicheng took Taiyuan, he sent envoys to urge surrender; Yunmao beheaded them and, with regional commander Zhou Yuji, held the city together. When it fell he killed himself, and his wife Yang drowned herself in a well.

sentences.zh: 孕懋，霸州人，進士。

translations.literal: Yunmao was a native of Bazhou and a jinshi graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Yunmao was from Bazhou and a jinshi graduate.

sentences.zh: 遇吉自有傳。

translations.literal: Yuji has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yuji has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 寧武失，賊破三關，犯大同。

translations.literal: Ningwu was lost; the bandits broke through the Three Passes and invaded Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Ningwu fell; the rebels broke through the Three Passes and marched on Datong.

sentences.zh: 衛景瑗，字仲玉，韓城人。

translations.literal: Wei Jingyuan, styled Zhongyu, was a native of Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jingyuan, courtesy name Zhongyu, was from Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士，授河南推官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi he became a jinshi and was appointed investigating censor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Tianqi and was appointed investigating censor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年征授御史，劾首輔周延儒納賄行私數事，復劾吏部侍郎曾楚卿憸邪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed censor; he impeached the chief grand secretary Zhou Yanru on several counts of taking bribes and acting privately, and again impeached the vice minister of personnel Zeng Chuqing for sycophancy and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was recalled and appointed censor. He impeached Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru for several counts of bribery and private dealings, and again impeached Vice Minister of Personnel Zeng Chuqing for sycophancy and corruption.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not act on the charges.

sentences.zh: 出按真定諸府。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect the prefectures of Zhending and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as a touring censor to inspect Zhending and the surrounding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 父喪，不俟命竟歸。

translations.literal: When his father died, he returned home without awaiting permission.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he went home without waiting for imperial leave.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 疏救給事中傅朝佑、李汝璨以論溫體仁下吏，故帝不懌，左遷行人司正。

translations.literal: He memorialized to save the supervising secretaries Fu Chaoyou and Li Ruocan, who had been arrested for criticizing Wen Tiren; for this the emperor was displeased and demoted him to chief of the courier service.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial to save Supervising Secretaries Fu Chaoyou and Li Ruocan, who had been imprisoned for criticizing Wen Tiren. The emperor took offense and demoted him to chief of the courier service.

sentences.zh: 歷尚寶、大理丞，進少卿。

translations.literal: He served as director of the imperial treasuries and as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and was promoted to vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the imperial treasuries and vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then was promoted to vice minister.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，擢右僉都御史，巡撫大同。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed governor of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifteenth year he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made governor of Datong.

sentences.zh: 歲饑疫，疏乞振濟。

translations.literal: In a year of famine and pestilence, he memorialized requesting relief.
translations.idiomatic: When famine and plague struck, he memorialized requesting relief funds.

sentences.zh: 搜軍實，練火器，戢豪宗，聲績甚著。

translations.literal: He investigated the army's true strength, drilled troops in firearms, restrained powerful clans, and won a very notable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He audited the army's strength, trained men in firearms, restrained powerful clans, and won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，李自成將犯山西，宣大總督王繼謨檄大同總兵官姜襄扼之河上，襄潛使納款而還。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year, Li Zicheng was about to invade Shanxi; Xuanda Grand Coordinator Wang Jimo ordered Datong regional commander Jiang Xiang to block him at the river, but Xiang secretly sent terms of surrender and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year, Li Zicheng was about to invade Shanxi. Xuanda Grand Coordinator Wang Jimo ordered Datong regional commander Jiang Xiang to block him at the river, but Xiang secretly sent terms of surrender and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景瑗不知其變也，及山西陷，景瑗邀襄歃血守。

translations.literal: Jingyuan knew nothing of this change; when Shanxi fell, Jingyuan invited Xiang to swear an oath of blood and jointly defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan knew nothing of this betrayal. After Shanxi fell, he invited Xiang to swear a blood oath and hold the city together.

sentences.zh: 襄出告人曰：「衛巡撫，秦人也，將應賊矣。

translations.literal: Xiang went out and told people: "Governor Wei is a man of Qin and is about to collude with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang went out and told people, "Governor Wei is a man of Qin and is about to collude with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 」代王疑之，不見景瑗，永慶王射殺景瑗仆。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Dai grew suspicious, refused to see Jingyuan, and the Prince of Yongqing shot and killed Jingyuan's servant.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Dai grew suspicious, refused to see Jingyuan, and the Prince of Yongqing shot and killed Jingyuan's servant.

sentences.zh: 會景瑗有足疾，不時出，兵事，襄主之。

translations.literal: As it happened Jingyuan had a foot ailment and did not go out regularly; military affairs were under Xiang's control.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan happened to suffer from a foot ailment and did not go out regularly, so military affairs fell under Xiang's control.

sentences.zh: 襄兄瑄，故昌平總兵也，勸襄降賊。

translations.literal: Xiang's elder brother Xuan, formerly regional commander at Changping, urged Xiang to surrender to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's elder brother Xuan, formerly regional commander at Changping, urged him to surrender to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 襄慮其下不從，人犒之銀，言勵守城將士，代王信之。

translations.literal: Xiang feared his men would not follow him, so he sent silver to reward the troops, saying it was to encourage the defenders—and the Prince of Dai believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang feared his men would not follow him, so he distributed silver to the troops, claiming it was to encourage the defenders—and the Prince of Dai believed him.

sentences.zh: 諸郡王分門守，襄每門遣卒二百人助守。

translations.literal: The various princes divided the gates for defense; at each gate Xiang sent two hundred men to help hold it.
translations.idiomatic: The various princes each defended a gate; at every gate Xiang posted two hundred men to assist.

sentences.zh: 至三月朔，賊抵城下。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month the bandits reached the foot of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month the rebels reached the city walls.

sentences.zh: 襄即射殺永慶王，開門迎賊入。

translations.literal: Xiang immediately shot and killed the Prince of Yongqing and opened the gate to welcome the bandits in.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang immediately shot and killed the Prince of Yongqing and opened the gates to welcome the rebels in.

sentences.zh: 紿景瑗計事，景瑗乘馬出，始知其變也，自墜馬下。

translations.literal: He deceived Jingyuan into coming out to discuss affairs; Jingyuan rode out on horseback and only then learned of the treachery, falling from his horse of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: He tricked Jingyuan into coming out to discuss strategy. Jingyuan rode out and only then learned of the betrayal, falling from his horse in shock.

sentences.zh: 賊執之見自成，自成欲官之。

translations.literal: The bandits seized him and brought him before Zicheng, who wished to give him office.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized him and brought him before Li Zicheng, who wanted to give him an official post.

sentences.zh: 景瑗據地坐，大呼皇帝而哭，賊義之，曰「忠臣也」，不殺。

translations.literal: Jingyuan sat on the ground, cried out to the emperor and wept; the bandits admired him, saying "A loyal minister," and did not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan sat on the ground, cried out to the emperor, and wept. The rebels admired him, saying "A loyal minister," and did not kill him.

sentences.zh: 景瑗猝起，以頭觸階石，血淋漓。

translations.literal: Jingyuan suddenly rose and struck his head against the step-stone until blood streamed down.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan suddenly rose and smashed his head against the step-stone until blood streamed down.

sentences.zh: 賊引出，顧見襄，罵曰：「反賊，與我盟而叛，神其赦汝耶！

translations.literal: The bandits led him out; turning he saw Xiang and cursed: "Traitor! You swore an oath with me and then betrayed me—will the spirits forgive you!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels led him out. Seeing Xiang, he cursed, "Traitor! You swore an oath with me and then betrayed me—will the spirits forgive you!

sentences.zh: 」賊使景瑗母勸之降。

translations.literal: " The bandits had Jingyuan's mother urge him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels had Jingyuan's mother urge him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 景瑗曰：「母年八十余矣，當自為計。

translations.literal: Jingyuan said: "Mother is more than eighty years old; you must think for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan said, "Mother is more than eighty years old; you must look after yourself.

sentences.zh: 兒，國大臣，不可以不死。

translations.literal: As for your son, a minister of state cannot fail to die.
translations.idiomatic: As for your son, a minister of state cannot fail to die.

sentences.zh: 」母出，景瑗謂人曰：「我不罵賊者，以全母也。

translations.literal: " When his mother had gone out, Jingyuan said to those around him: "The reason I did not curse the bandits was to protect my mother.
translations.idiomatic: " After his mother left, Jingyuan said to those around him, "The reason I did not curse the rebels was to protect my mother.

sentences.zh: 」初六日自縊於僧寺。

translations.literal: " On the sixth he hanged himself in a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: " On the sixth he hanged himself in a Buddhist temple.

sentences.zh: 賊嘆曰：「忠臣！

translations.literal: The bandits sighed and said: "A loyal minister!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sighed and said, "A loyal minister!

sentences.zh: 」移其妻子空舍，戒毋犯。

translations.literal: " They moved his wife and children to an empty house and ordered that they must not be molested.
translations.idiomatic: " They moved his wife and children to an empty house and ordered that they must not be harmed.

sentences.zh: 殺代王傳齊及其宗室殆盡。

translations.literal: They killed the Prince of Dai Zhu Chuanji and nearly wiped out the princely clan.
translations.idiomatic: They killed the Prince of Dai Zhu Chuanji and nearly exterminated the princely clan.

sentences.zh: 分巡副使朱家仕，盡驅妻妾子女入井，而己從之，死者十有六人。

translations.literal: Assistant commissioner for circuit patrol Zhu Jiashi drove all his wives, concubines, and children into a well and then followed them; sixteen people died.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant commissioner for circuit patrol Zhu Jiashi drove all his wives, concubines, and children into a well and then followed them; sixteen people died.

sentences.zh: 督儲郎中徐有聲、山陰知縣李倬亦死之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary for grain storage Xu Yousheng and Li Chuo, magistrate of Shanyin, also died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary for grain storage Xu Yousheng and Li Chuo, magistrate of Shanyin, also died.

sentences.zh: 諸生李若蔡自題其壁曰：「一門完節」，一家九人自經。

translations.literal: The licentiate Li Ruocai inscribed on his wall: "A household of complete integrity"; nine people of one family hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The licentiate Li Ruocai wrote on his wall, "A household of complete integrity"; nine members of one family hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 家仕，河州人。

translations.literal: Jiashi was a native of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashi was from Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈景瑗兵部尚書，謚忠毅。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, Jingyuan was posthumously given the title Minister of War and the posthumous name Zhongyi ("Steadfast and Resolute").
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Jingyuan was posthumously made Minister of War with the posthumous name Zhongyi ("Steadfast and Resolute").

sentences.zh: 賊既陷大同，以兵徇陽和，長驅向宣府。

translations.literal: After the bandits had taken Datong, they marched troops through Yanghe and drove straight toward Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels took Datong, they marched through Yanghe and drove straight toward Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 朱之馮，字樂三，大興人。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhifeng, styled Lesan, was a native of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhifeng, courtesy name Lesan, was from Daxing.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，榷稅河西務。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and collected customs duties at Hexiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and collected transit duties at Hexiwu.

sentences.zh: 課贏，貯公帑無所私。

translations.literal: His collections exceeded the quota, yet he stored the surplus in the public treasury without private gain.
translations.idiomatic: His collections exceeded the quota, yet he deposited the surplus in the public treasury without keeping anything for himself.

sentences.zh: 以外艱去。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning for his wife's father.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his wife's father.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年起故官，進員外郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was recalled to his former office and promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongzhen he was recalled to his former post and promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 坐罣誤，謫浙江布政司理問。

translations.literal: For a technical error he was demoted to judicial assistant in the Zhejiang provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: For a procedural error he was demoted to judicial assistant in the Zhejiang provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 稍遷行人司副，歷刑部郎中，浙江驛傳僉事，青州參議。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to vice chief of the courier service, then served as bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, assistant commissioner for courier stations in Zhejiang, and vice commissioner of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to vice chief of the courier service, then served as bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, assistant commissioner for courier stations in Zhejiang, and vice commissioner of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 盜劫沂水民，株連甚眾。

translations.literal: Bandits robbed the people of Yishui, and very many were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits robbed the people of Yishui, and a great many innocents were implicated.

sentences.zh: 之馮捕得真盜，大獄盡解。

translations.literal: Zhifeng captured the real bandits and the great case was entirely resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifeng captured the real bandits and the entire case was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 擒治樂安土豪李中行，權貴為請，不聽。

translations.literal: He arrested and punished the local tyrant Li Zhongxing of Le'an; powerful men interceded for him, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He arrested and punished the local tyrant Li Zhongxing of Le'an. Powerful men interceded for him, but Zhifeng refused.

sentences.zh: 進副使，賫表入都，寄家屬濟南。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice commissioner, he carried a memorial to the capital and left his family in Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice commissioner, he carried a memorial to the capital and left his family in Jinan.

sentences.zh: 濟南破，妻馮匿姑及子於他所，而自沈於井。

translations.literal: When Jinan fell, his wife Feng hid his mother and son elsewhere and drowned herself in a well.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinan fell, his wife Feng hid his mother and son elsewhere, then drowned herself in a well.

sentences.zh: 姑李聞之，為絕粒而死。

translations.literal: His mother Li, hearing of it, stopped eating and died.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Li, hearing of it, starved herself to death.

sentences.zh: 柩還，之馮廬墓側三年。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, Zhifeng mourned at the tomb for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin returned, Zhifeng lived by the tomb in mourning for three years.

sentences.zh: 起河東副使。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as vice commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as vice commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 河東大猾朱全宇潛通秦賊，之馮至則執殺之，部內以寧。

translations.literal: The great rogue Zhu Quanyu of Hedong had secretly communicated with the Qin bandits; when Zhifeng arrived he arrested and executed him, and the region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The great rogue Zhu Quanyu of Hedong had secretly communicated with the Shaanxi rebels; when Zhifeng arrived he arrested and executed him, and the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 之馮自妻死不再娶，亦不置妾媵，一室蕭然。

translations.literal: After his wife's death Zhifeng never remarried and kept no concubines; his household was austere and bare.
translations.idiomatic: After his wife's death Zhifeng never remarried and kept no concubines; his household was spare and austere.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，擢右僉都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed governor of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth year he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made governor of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 司餉主事張碩抱以克餉激變，群縛碩抱。

translations.literal: Zhang Shuobao, chief secretary for provisions, provoked a mutiny by withholding rations; the men bound him in a body.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuobao, chief secretary for provisions, provoked a mutiny by withholding rations, and the men bound him en masse.

sentences.zh: 之馮出撫諭，貸商民貲給散，而密捕誅首惡七人，劾碩抱下吏。

translations.literal: Zhifeng went out to calm and instruct them, borrowed merchants' funds to distribute, secretly arrested and executed seven ringleaders, and impeached Shuobao, sending him to the magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifeng went out to calm them, borrowed funds from merchants to distribute, secretly arrested and executed seven ringleaders, and impeached Shuobao, sending him to the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 軍情帖然。

translations.literal: Military morale settled.
translations.idiomatic: Military morale settled.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，李自成陷大同。

translations.literal: The next year in the third month Li Zicheng took Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the third month, Li Zicheng took Datong.

sentences.zh: 之馮集將吏於城樓，設高皇帝位，歃血誓死守，懸賞格勵將士。

translations.literal: Zhifeng gathered officers on the tower, set up a seat for the High Emperor, swore an oath of blood to defend to the death, and posted reward standards to encourage the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifeng gathered officers on the city tower, set up a seat for the High Emperor, swore a blood oath to defend to the death, and posted reward notices to encourage the troops.

sentences.zh: 而人心已散，監視中官杜勛且與總兵王承允爭先納款矣，見之馮叩頭，請以城下賊。

translations.literal: But hearts were already scattered; the supervising eunuch Du Xun and the regional commander Wang Chengyun were already racing to surrender first. When they saw Zhifeng they kowtowed and asked to hand the city over to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: But morale had already collapsed. Supervising eunuch Du Xun and regional commander Wang Chengyun were already racing to surrender first. When they saw Zhifeng they kowtowed and asked to hand the city over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 之馮大罵曰：「勛，爾帝所倚信，特遣爾，以封疆屬爾，爾至即通賊，何面目見帝！

translations.literal: Zhifeng cursed loudly: "Xun, the emperor relied on and trusted you and specially sent you here, entrusting the borderland to you—and the moment you arrived you colluded with bandits; what face have you to show the emperor!
translations.idiomatic: Zhifeng cursed loudly, "Xun, the emperor relied on and trusted you and specially sent you here, entrusting the frontier to you—and the moment you arrived you colluded with rebels. What face have you to show the emperor!

sentences.zh: 」勛不答，笑而去。

translations.literal: " Xun made no reply and left with a laugh.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun made no reply and walked off laughing.

sentences.zh: 俄賊且至，勛蟒袍鳴騶，郊迎三十里之外，將士皆散。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits were about to arrive; Xun, in python robes with outriders clearing the way, went thirty li beyond the suburbs to welcome them, and officers and soldiers all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels were about to arrive. Xun, in python robes with outriders clearing the way, went thirty li beyond the suburbs to welcome them, and officers and soldiers all scattered.

sentences.zh: 之馮登城太息，見大炮，語左右：「為我發之！

translations.literal: Zhifeng climbed the wall and sighed deeply; seeing the great cannon, he said to those beside him: "Fire it for me!
translations.idiomatic: Zhifeng climbed the wall and sighed deeply. Seeing the great cannon, he said to those beside him, "Fire it for me!

sentences.zh: 」默無應者。

translations.literal: " There was silence; no one responded.
translations.idiomatic: " There was silence; no one responded.

sentences.zh: 自起爇火，則炮孔丁塞，或從後掣其肘。

translations.literal: He rose to light the fuse himself, but the touchhole was plugged tight, and someone pulled his elbow from behind.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to light the fuse himself, but the touchhole was plugged tight, and someone pulled his elbow from behind.

sentences.zh: 之馮撫膺嘆曰：「不意人心至此！

translations.literal: Zhifeng clutched his chest and sighed: "I never expected hearts could sink so low!
translations.idiomatic: Zhifeng clutched his chest and sighed, "I never expected morale could sink so low!

sentences.zh: 」仰天大哭。

translations.literal: " He looked up to heaven and wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: " He looked up to heaven and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 賊至城下，承允開門入之，訛言賊不殺人，且免徭賦，則舉城嘩然皆喜，結彩焚香以迎。

translations.literal: When the bandits reached the foot of the wall, Chengyun opened the gate and let them in; false reports that the bandits would not kill and would exempt corvée and taxes made the whole city burst into clamorous joy, decking the streets and burning incense to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels reached the walls, Chengyun opened the gates and let them in. Rumors that the rebels would not kill and would exempt corvée and taxes sent the whole city into clamorous joy; people hung decorations and burned incense to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 左右欲擁之馮出走，之馮叱之，乃南向叩頭，草遺表，勸帝收人心，厲士節，自縊而死。

translations.literal: Those beside him tried to hustle Zhifeng away, but he rebuked them; then facing south he kowtowed, drafted a death memorial urging the emperor to win men's hearts and stiffen soldiers' integrity, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Those beside him tried to hustle Zhifeng away, but he rebuked them. Then facing south he kowtowed, drafted a death memorial urging the emperor to win men's hearts and stiffen soldiers' integrity, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 賊棄屍濠中，濠旁犬日食人屍，獨之馮無損也。

translations.literal: The bandits threw his corpse into the moat; dogs beside the moat daily ate human corpses, yet Zhifeng alone was untouched.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threw his corpse into the moat. Dogs beside the moat daily ate human corpses, yet Zhifeng alone was untouched.

sentences.zh: 同日死者，督糧通判朱敏泰、諸生姚時中、副將寧龍及系獄總兵官董用文、副將劉九卿及裏居知縣申以孝，其他婦女死義者又十余人。

translations.literal: On the same day Zhu Mintai, grain transport intendant; Yao Shizhong, licentiate; Ning Long, vice general; Dong Yongwen, regional commander held in prison; Liu Jiuqing, vice general; and Shen Yixiao, magistrate living at home, also died; more than ten other women died for righteousness as well.
translations.idiomatic: On the same day Zhu Mintai, grain transport intendant; Yao Shizhong, licentiate; Ning Long, vice general; Dong Yongwen, regional commander held in prison; Liu Jiuqing, vice general; and Shen Yixiao, magistrate living at home, also died; more than ten other women died for righteousness as well.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈之馮兵部尚書，謚忠壯。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, Zhifeng was posthumously given the title Minister of War and the posthumous name Zhongzhuang ("Loyal and Stalwart").
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Zhifeng was posthumously made Minister of War with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang ("Loyal and Stalwart").

sentences.zh: 勛既降賊，從攻京師，射書於城中。

translations.literal: After Xun had surrendered to the bandits, he followed them in attacking the capital and shot letters into the city.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun surrendered to the rebels, he followed them in attacking the capital and shot letters into the city.

sentences.zh: 城中初聞勛死宣府，帝為予贈蔭立祠，至是以為鬼。

translations.literal: The city had first heard that Xun died at Xuanfu, and the emperor had granted posthumous honors and established a shrine; now they took him for a ghost.
translations.idiomatic: The city had first heard that Xun died at Xuanfu, and the emperor had granted posthumous honors and established a shrine for him; now they took him for a ghost.

sentences.zh: 守城監王承恩倚女墻而與語，縋勛入見帝，盛稱自成，「上可自為計」。

translations.literal: City-defending supervisor Wang Chengen leaned on the parapet and spoke with him; they lowered Xun on a rope to see the emperor, who lavishly praised Zicheng, saying "Your Majesty may decide for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: City-defending supervisor Wang Chengen leaned on the parapet and spoke with him. They lowered Xun on a rope to see the emperor, who lavishly praised Li Zicheng, saying "Your Majesty may decide for yourself."

sentences.zh: 復縋之出，笑語諸守監曰：「吾輩富貴自在也。」

translations.literal: They lowered him out again; laughing he said to the other defending supervisors: "Our wealth and rank are ours to enjoy."
translations.idiomatic: They lowered him out again. Laughing, he said to the other defending supervisors, "Our wealth and rank are ours to enjoy."

sentences.zh: 陳士奇，字平人，漳浦人也。

translations.literal: Chen Shiqi, styled Pingren, was a native of Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shiqi, courtesy name Pingren, was from Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 好學，有文名，不知兵。

translations.literal: He loved learning, had a literary reputation, and knew nothing of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, had a literary reputation, and knew nothing of warfare.

sentences.zh: 舉天啟五年進士，授中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a drafting secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Tianqi and was appointed a drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年考選，授禮部主事，擢廣西提學僉事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen, in the qualifying examination he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Rites and promoted to assistant commissioner for education in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen, in the qualifying examination he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Rites and promoted to assistant commissioner for education in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起重慶兵備，尋改貴州，復督學政。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he was recalled to military preparations at Chongqing; soon he was transferred to Guizhou and again supervised educational administration.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he was recalled to military preparations at Chongqing; soon he was transferred to Guizhou and again supervised educational administration.

sentences.zh: 母憂闋，起贛州兵備參議，進副使，督四川學政。

translations.literal: When the mourning for his mother ended, he was called up as military preparations consultant at Ganzhou, promoted to vice commissioner, and supervised Sichuan educational administration.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning for his mother ended, he was recalled to serve as military preparations commissioner at Ganzhou, promoted to vice commissioner, and put in charge of Sichuan's educational administration.

sentences.zh: 廷臣交章薦士奇知兵。

translations.literal: Court officials submitted memorials one after another recommending that Shiqi understood military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at court submitted memorial after memorial praising Shiqi's military expertise.

sentences.zh: 十五年秋，擢右僉都御史，代廖大奇巡撫四川。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifteenth year, he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, replacing Liao Daqi as governor of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed governor of Sichuan in place of Liao Daqi.

sentences.zh: 松潘兵變，眾數萬，士奇諭以禍福，鹹就撫。

translations.literal: At Songpan a military mutiny broke out with tens of thousands of men; Shiqi explained fortune and misfortune to them, and all submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: When a mutiny erupted at Songpan among tens of thousands of troops, Shiqi reasoned with them about the consequences of their actions, and they all accepted pacification.

sentences.zh: 搖、黃賊十三家，縱橫川東北十余年，殺掠軍民無算；

translations.literal: Thirteen bands of Yao and Huang bandits had rampaged across northeastern Sichuan for more than ten years, killing and plundering soldiers and civilians beyond count;
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen Yao and Huang bandit bands had terrorized northeastern Sichuan for more than a decade, slaughtering and plundering soldiers and civilians without number;

sentences.zh: 執少壯，文其面為軍，至數十萬。

translations.literal: they seized the young and strong, tattooed their faces to make soldiers, reaching hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: they seized the young and able-bodied, marked their faces with tattoos to press them into service, and amassed forces numbering in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 士奇檄副使陳其赤、葛征奇，參將趙榮貴等進討，屢告捷。

translations.literal: Shiqi dispatched orders to Vice Commissioners Chen Qichi and Ge Zhengqi and Assistant General Zhao Ronggui and others to advance and attack, repeatedly reporting victories.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi ordered Vice Commissioners Chen Qichi and Ge Zhengqi and Assistant General Zhao Ronggui and others to march against them, and victory reports came in again and again.

sentences.zh: 而賊狡，迄不能制。

translations.literal: But the bandits were cunning, and in the end they could not be subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the bandits were cunning, and in the end he could not bring them under control.

sentences.zh: 士奇本文人，再督學政，好與諸生談兵，朝士以士奇知兵。

translations.literal: Shiqi was originally a man of letters; having twice supervised educational administration, he liked to discuss military affairs with students, and court officials considered Shiqi knowledgeable in warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was a scholar by training. Having twice overseen the provincial examinations, he enjoyed debating military strategy with students, and court officials came to believe he understood warfare.

sentences.zh: 及秉節鉞，反以文墨為事，軍政廢弛。

translations.literal: When he came to hold military authority, he instead occupied himself with literary matters, and military administration fell into neglect.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held real military authority, he devoted himself to literary pursuits instead, and military administration lapsed into disorder.

sentences.zh: 石砫女將秦良玉嘗圖全蜀形勢，請益兵分守十三隘，扼賊奔突。

translations.literal: Shizhu's female general Qin Liangyu once mapped the overall situation of all Sichuan, requesting additional troops to garrison the thirteen passes separately and block the bandits' raids.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Liangyu, the female general of Shizhu, once drew up a map of Sichuan's overall strategic situation and asked for reinforcements to hold the thirteen mountain passes, cutting off the bandits' avenues of attack.

sentences.zh: 置不問，蜀以是擾。

translations.literal: He ignored it, and Sichuan was thus disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He paid no attention, and Sichuan was thrown into turmoil as a result.

sentences.zh: 明年十二月，朝議以其不任，命龍文光代之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the next year, the court decided he was unfit for the task and ordered Long Wenguang to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the following year, the court judged him unfit for the post and ordered Long Wenguang to replace him.

sentences.zh: 士奇方候代，而陽平將趙光遠擁兵二萬，護瑞王常浩自漢中來奔，士民避難者又數萬，至保寧，蜀人震駭。

translations.literal: Shiqi was awaiting replacement when Yangping General Zhao Guangyuan led twenty thousand troops, escorting Prince of Rui Chang Hao fleeing from Hanzhong, and tens of thousands more commoners fleeing disaster also arrived at Baoning; the people of Sichuan were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was awaiting his successor when Yangping General Zhao Guangyuan arrived with twenty thousand troops, escorting Prince of Rui Chang Hao in flight from Hanzhong, followed by tens of thousands of refugees. When they reached Baoning, all of Sichuan was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 士奇馳責光遠曰：「若退守陽平關，為吾捍衛，不惜二萬金犒軍。

translations.literal: Shiqi rode quickly to rebuke Guangyuan, saying: "If you withdraw to guard Yangping Pass and defend for me, I will not spare twenty thousand taels of gold to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi rode posthaste to rebuke Guangyuan. "Withdraw to Yangping Pass and hold the line for me," he said, "and I will not hesitate to spend twenty thousand taels of gold to reward your troops.

sentences.zh: 如頓此，需厚餉，吾頭可斷，餉不可得也。

translations.literal: If you stay here and demand generous provisions, my head may be cut off, but provisions you shall not get."
translations.idiomatic: But if you linger here and demand heavy rations, you may have my head — yet you will not get your provisions."

sentences.zh: 」光遠退屯陽平，王以三千騎奔重慶。

translations.literal: Guangyuan withdrew to encamp at Yangping; the prince fled to Chongqing with three thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan withdrew to Yangping, while the prince rode to Chongqing with three thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，文光受代，士奇將行，京師告變。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year, Wenguang accepted the transfer; as Shiqi was about to depart, the capital reported calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year, Wenguang took up the post, and just as Shiqi prepared to leave, word arrived that catastrophe had struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 士奇自以知兵也，曰：「必報國仇。

translations.literal: Shiqi, considering himself knowledgeable in military affairs, said: "I must avenge the nation."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi, who still regarded himself as a man who understood war, declared, "I must avenge the nation."

sentences.zh: 」遂留駐重慶，遣水師參將曾英擊賊於忠州，焚其舟；

translations.literal: So he remained stationed at Chongqing, sending Naval Assistant General Zeng Ying to attack bandits at Zhongzhou and burn their boats;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore remained at Chongqing, dispatching Naval Assistant General Zeng Ying to strike the rebels at Zhongzhou and burn their fleet;

sentences.zh: 遣趙榮貴禦賊於梁山。

translations.literal: he sent Zhao Ronggui to defend against bandits at Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: and sending Zhao Ronggui to hold the rebels at bay at Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 獻忠由葫蘆壩左步右騎，翼舟而上，二將敗奔，遂奪佛圖關，陷涪州。

translations.literal: Xianzhong advanced via Hulu Ba with infantry on the left and cavalry on the right, boats flanking upstream; the two generals were defeated and fled, and he seized Fotu Pass and captured Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong advanced through Hulu Ba with infantry on the left flank and cavalry on the right, his boats moving upstream in support. Both generals were routed and fled, and Xianzhong seized Fotu Pass and took Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 士奇征石砫援兵不至。

translations.literal: Shiqi called for reinforcements from Shizhu, but aid did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi called on Shizhu for reinforcements, but none came.

sentences.zh: 或勸：「公已謝事，宜去。

translations.literal: Someone advised: "You have already retired from office; you should leave."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him, "Your term of office is already over — you ought to go."

sentences.zh: 」士奇不可。

translations.literal: Shiqi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi refused.

sentences.zh: 賊抵城下，擊以滾炮，賊死無數。

translations.literal: When the bandits reached the city walls, rolling cannon fire was used against them, and countless bandits died.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels reached the walls, the defenders answered with rolling cannon fire, and the dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 二十日夜，黑雲四布，賊穴地轟城。

translations.literal: On the night of the twentieth, black clouds spread everywhere; the bandits tunneled underground and blasted the walls.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth, black clouds blotted out the sky. The rebels tunneled beneath the walls and set off explosions.

sentences.zh: 城陷，王、士奇及副使陳糸熏、知府王行儉、知縣王錫俱被執。

translations.literal: The city fell; the prince, Shiqi, Vice Commissioner Chen Xi, Prefect Wang Xingjian, and Magistrate Wang Xi were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell. The prince, Shiqi, Vice Commissioner Chen Xi, Prefect Wang Xingjian, and Magistrate Wang Xi were all taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 士奇大罵，賊縛於教場，將殺之，忽雷雨晦冥，咫尺不見。

translations.literal: Shiqi cursed loudly; the bandits bound him at the drill ground and were about to kill him when suddenly thunder and rain made the sky dark, and one could not see within arm's reach.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi rained curses upon them. The rebels bound him on the drill ground and were about to execute him when thunder and rain suddenly blotted out the sky, so that one could not see an arm's length ahead.

sentences.zh: 獻忠仰而詬曰：「我殺人，何與天事！

translations.literal: Xianzhong looked up and cursed, saying: "I kill people — what has that to do with Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong looked up and railed at the sky: "I kill men — what business is that of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」用大炮向天叢擊。

translations.literal: He fired cannons en masse toward the sky.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his great guns fired in volleys toward the heavens.

sentences.zh: 俄晴霽，遂肆僇。

translations.literal: Soon the sky cleared, and the slaughter began.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the sky cleared, and the massacre proceeded.

sentences.zh: 士奇罵不絕口而死，王亦遇害，賊集軍民三萬七千余人，斫其臂。

translations.literal: Shiqi died cursing without cease; the prince was also killed; the bandits gathered more than thirty-seven thousand soldiers and civilians and chopped off their arms.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi died still cursing. The prince was killed as well. The rebels then assembled more than thirty-seven thousand soldiers and civilians and hacked off their arms.

sentences.zh: 遂犯成都。

translations.literal: Then they invaded Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: They then marched on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 糸熏，本關南兵備副使，護瑞王入蜀，及於難。

translations.literal: Chen Xi had originally been vice commissioner of military preparations for Guannan; he escorted the Prince of Rui into Sichuan and perished in the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xi had formerly served as vice commissioner of military preparations for Guannan and had escorted the Prince of Rui into Sichuan; he too perished in the catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 行儉，字質行，宜興人。

translations.literal: Xingjian, courtesy name Zhixing, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingjian, styled Zhixing, was a native of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年進士，守重慶，善撫馭，為賊臠死。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the tenth year of Chongzhen, he defended Chongqing, was skilled at governing and control, and was torn apart and killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the tenth year of Chongzhen, he held Chongqing and governed with skill and compassion, yet was dismembered and killed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 錫，新建人，崇禎十三年進士，除巴縣知縣。

translations.literal: Xi was a native of Xinjian, a jinshi of the thirteenth year of Chongzhen, appointed magistrate of Ba County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi was a native of Xinjian and a jinshi of the thirteenth year of Chongzhen, appointed magistrate of Ba County.

sentences.zh: 嘗從士奇殲土寇彭長庚之黨，又斬搖、黃賊魁馬超。

translations.literal: He had once followed Shiqi in annihilating the followers of the local bandit Peng Changgeng, and also beheaded the Yao-Huang bandit chieftain Ma Chao.
translations.idiomatic: He had once served under Shiqi in wiping out the band of the local outlaw Peng Changgeng and had also beheaded Ma Chao, chieftain of the Yao and Huang rebels.

sentences.zh: 至是，賊蒙巨板穴城，錫灌以熱油，多死。

translations.literal: At this time the bandits covered themselves with huge planks and tunneled under the walls; Xi poured hot oil on them, and many died.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion the rebels shielded themselves with massive planks as they tunneled beneath the walls; Xi poured boiling oil on them, and many perished.

sentences.zh: 及被執，大罵，抉其齒，罵不已。

translations.literal: When captured, he cursed loudly; they pried out his teeth, yet he did not stop cursing.
translations.idiomatic: Once taken, he cursed them without restraint. They pried out his teeth, yet still he would not stop.

sentences.zh: 捶膝使跪，益仡立。

translations.literal: They beat his knees to make him kneel, but he stood even more upright.
translations.idiomatic: They struck his knees to force him to kneel, but he stood all the more rigidly upright.

sentences.zh: 舁至教場，縛樹上射之，又臠而烙之。

translations.literal: They carried him to the drill ground, bound him to a tree and shot him, then dismembered and branded him.
translations.idiomatic: They carried him to the drill ground, bound him to a tree, and shot him; then they carved up his body and seared it with hot irons.

sentences.zh: 既死，復毀其骨。

translations.literal: After he died, they destroyed his bones as well.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he was dead, they smashed his bones.

sentences.zh: 指揮顧景聞城陷，入瑞王府，以己所乘馬乘王，鞭而走，遇賊呼曰：「賊寧殺我，無犯帝子。

translations.literal: Commander Gu Jingwen, when the city fell, entered the Prince of Rui's residence, put the prince on his own horse, whipped it and fled; encountering bandits he cried: "Bandits, kill me if you will, but do not harm the emperor's son."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Commander Gu Jingwen entered the residence of the Prince of Rui, placed the prince on his own horse, and lashed it into a gallop. Encountering rebels, he shouted, "Kill me if you must, but do not lay a hand on the emperor's son!"

sentences.zh: 」賊刺殺王，景遂死之。

translations.literal: The bandits stabbed and killed the prince; Jingwen then died for him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stabbed the prince to death, and Jingwen died defending him.

sentences.zh: 龍文光，馬平人，天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: Long Wenguang, a native of Maping, was a jinshi of the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Long Wenguang was a native of Maping and a jinshi of the second year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十七年，以川北參政擢右僉都御史，代陳士奇巡撫四川。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, as Sichuan North Administration Commissioner he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, replacing Chen Shiqi as governor of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, while serving as administration commissioner for northern Sichuan, he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed governor of Sichuan in Chen Shiqi's place.

sentences.zh: 聞命，與總兵官劉佳引率兵三千，由順慶馳赴之。

translations.literal: Upon receiving the appointment, together with Commander-in-Chief Liu Jiayin he led three thousand troops, rushing from Shunqing to the scene.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving the appointment, he and Commander Liu Jiayin led three thousand troops posthaste from Shunqing toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 部署未定，數日而城陷。

translations.literal: Before deployment was settled, within days the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before their dispositions were even complete, the city fell within days.

sentences.zh: 賊盡驅文武將吏及軍民男婦於東門之外，將戮之，忽有龍尾下垂，賊以為瑞，遂停刑。

translations.literal: The bandits drove all civil and military officials and soldiers and civilians, men and women, outside the east gate to be executed; suddenly a dragon's tail descended, and the bandits took it as an auspicious sign and halted the execution.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels herded every civil and military official, soldier, and civilian — men and women alike — outside the east gate to be slaughtered. Suddenly a dragon's tail appeared descending from the sky; the rebels took it as an omen of good fortune and stayed the execution.

sentences.zh: 文光、佳引卒不屈，賊殺文光於濯錦橋，佳引自投於浣花溪。

translations.literal: Wenguang and Jiayin refused to submit to the end; the bandits killed Wenguang at Zhuojin Bridge, and Jiayin threw himself into Huanhua Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Wenguang and Jiayin would not yield to the end. The rebels killed Wenguang at Zhuojin Bridge, and Jiayin drowned himself in Huanhua Stream.

sentences.zh: 劉之勃，字安侯，鳳翔人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhibo, courtesy name Anhou, was a native of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhibo, styled Anhou, was a native of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年進士。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi of the seventh year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授行人，擢御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier and promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier and later promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 上節財六議，言：「先朝馬萬計，草場止五六所，今馬漸少，場反增二倍，可節省者一。

translations.literal: He submitted six proposals for economizing expenditures, saying: "In former times horses numbered in the tens of thousands, with only five or six pasture grounds; now horses gradually decrease while pastures have doubled — this may be economized, the first item.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted six proposals for fiscal restraint, writing: "In earlier reigns the imperial stables held tens of thousands of horses across no more than five or six pasture grounds; today the horses grow fewer while the pastures have doubled — here is one area for savings.

sentences.zh: 水衡工役費，歲幾百萬，近奉明旨，朝廷不事興作，而節慎庫額數襲為常，可節省者二。

translations.literal: Waterworks labor costs reach nearly millions per year; recently an imperial edict was received that the court would not undertake construction, yet the Jieshen Treasury allocations continue by rote — this may be economized, the second item.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditure on palace construction runs to nearly a million taels a year. The throne has lately decreed that the court shall undertake no new building projects, yet the Jieshen Treasury continues to disburse funds as before — here is a second area for savings.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮兵馬時敗潰而餉額不減，虛伍必多，可節省者三。

translations.literal: Garrison troops of various posts are often defeated and routed while ration quotas remain undiminished; phantom rolls must be numerous — this may be economized, the third item.
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons of the frontier posts are repeatedly routed in battle, yet their pay quotas remain unchanged; ghost soldiers on the rolls must be legion — here is a third area for savings.

sentences.zh: 光祿宴享賜賚，大抵從簡，而監局廚役多冗濫，可節省者四。

translations.literal: Imperial Household feasts and gifts are generally kept simple, yet supervisory offices' kitchen servants are many and superfluous — this may be economized, the fourth item.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household's banquets and gifts are already kept frugal, yet the kitchens and staffs of the supervisory bureaus are bloated with redundant personnel — here is a fourth area for savings.

sentences.zh: 三吳織造，澤、潞機杼，以及香蠟、藥材、陶器，無歲不貢，積之內為廢物，輸之下皆金錢，可節省者五。

translations.literal: Three Wu weaving, Ze-Lu looms, as well as incense, wax, medicinal materials, and pottery — tribute is sent every year without fail; what accumulates within becomes waste, what is shipped below is all silver — this may be economized, the fifth item.
translations.idiomatic: Silks from the Three Wu region, looms from Ze and Lu, and tribute of incense, wax, medicinal herbs, and pottery arrive every year without fail. Within the palace they pile up as useless clutter; below they drain the treasury of silver — here is a fifth area for savings.

sentences.zh: 軍前監紀、監軍、贊畫之官，不可勝紀，平時則以一人而縻千百人之餉，臨敵又以千百人而衛一人之身，耗食兼耗兵，可節省者六。

translations.literal: Camp observers, military supervisors, and strategic planning officers are beyond counting; in peacetime one man ties up the rations of hundreds and thousands, in battle hundreds and thousands guard one man's person — wasting food and wasting soldiers alike — this may be economized, the sixth item.
translations.idiomatic: Camp inspectors, army supervisors, and strategic advisers in the field are beyond numbering. In peacetime a single officer consumes the rations of hundreds; in battle hundreds guard one man's person. Food and fighting strength are wasted together — here is a sixth area for savings.

sentences.zh: 」又疏陳東廠三弊，言：「東廠司緝訪，而內五城，外巡按，以及刑部、大理皆不能舉其職，此不便於官守。

translations.literal: He also memorialized three abuses of the Eastern Depot, saying: "The Eastern Depot handles investigation, yet within the Five Cities and without the touring censors, as well as the Ministry of Justice and Court of Review, none can perform their duties — this is inconvenient for official administration.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial on three abuses of the Eastern Depot, writing: "The Eastern Depot has charge of investigation and arrest, yet the Five Cities within the capital, the touring censors in the provinces, and even the Ministry of Justice and Court of Review cannot perform their own duties — this is an affront to the regular order of government.

sentences.zh: 奸民千里首告，假捏姓名，一紙株連，萬金立罄，此不便於民生。

translations.literal: Wicked commoners denounce from a thousand li away, fabricating names; one document implicates all, and ten thousand taels are instantly exhausted — this is inconvenient for the people's livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Malicious informers denounce others from a thousand li away, inventing names at will; a single accusation can ruin an entire clan and drain ten thousand taels in an instant — this is an affliction upon the people's livelihood.

sentences.zh: 子弟訐父兄，奴仆訐家主，部民訐官長，東廠皆樂聞，此不便於國體。

translations.literal: Sons denounce fathers and elder brothers, servants denounce masters, subjects denounce officials — the Eastern Depot delights in hearing all of it — this is inconvenient for the state's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Sons accuse their fathers and elder brothers, servants accuse their masters, commoners accuse their magistrates — and the Eastern Depot welcomes every such report. This is a stain upon the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 」帝皆納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted every one of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 十五年出按四川。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he went out to inspect Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was dispatched to conduct an inspection tour of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十六年秋，類報災異，請緩賦省刑，亦弭災一術，時不能用。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixteenth year, calamities and portents were reported in succession; he requested tax relief and reduced punishments, noting that these are also means to quell disasters — the court could not adopt them at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixteenth year, reports of calamities and portents poured in one after another. He petitioned for tax relief and lighter punishments, arguing that these too were means to still the heavens' wrath — but the court could not act on his advice.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，張獻忠大破川中郡邑。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, Zhang Xianzhong thoroughly routed prefectures and counties in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, Zhang Xianzhong smashed one prefecture and county after another across Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四月，聞都城失守，人心益恟懼。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, upon hearing the capital had fallen, people's hearts grew increasingly panic-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, when word came that the capital had fallen, panic spread through every heart.

sentences.zh: 舉人楊鏘、劉道貞等謀擁蜀王至澍監國，之勃不可，躍入池中，議乃寢。

translations.literal: Juren Yang Qiang, Liu Daozhen and others plotted to install Prince of Shu Zhi Shu as regent; Zhibo refused, leaped into a pond, and the plan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The juren Yang Qiang, Liu Daozhen, and others plotted to install Prince of Shu Zhi Shu as regent. Zhibo would not countenance it and leaped into a pond; the scheme was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊逼成都，之勃與巡撫龍文光、建昌兵備副使劉士鬥等分陴拒守，總兵官劉鎮藩出戰而敗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, bandits pressed upon Chengdu; Zhibo together with Governor Long Wenguang, Jianchang Military Vice Commissioner Liu Shidou and others defended from various ramparts; Commander Liu Zhenfan went out to battle and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the rebels closed in on Chengdu. Zhibo, together with Governor Long Wenguang, Jianchang Vice Commissioner Liu Shidou, and others, manned the ramparts in a divided defense. Commander Liu Zhenfan sallied forth and was routed.

sentences.zh: 賊穴城，實以火藥；

translations.literal: The bandits tunneled under the walls, filling with gunpowder;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dug tunnels beneath the walls and packed them with gunpowder;

sentences.zh: 又刳大木長數丈者合之，纏以帛，貯藥，向城樓。

translations.literal: they also hollowed out great logs several zhang long, joined them together, wrapped them in silk, stored gunpowder, and aimed them at the tower.
translations.idiomatic: they also hollowed out logs several zhang in length, fitted them together, wrapped them in cloth, loaded them with explosives, and aimed them at the gate towers.

sentences.zh: 之勃厲眾奮擊，賊卻二三里，皆喜，以為將去也。

translations.literal: Zhibo encouraged the troops to strike fiercely; the bandits retreated two or three li; all rejoiced, thinking they were about to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibo roused the defenders to a fierce counterattack, and the rebels fell back two or three li. Everyone rejoiced, believing the siege was lifting.

sentences.zh: 初九日黎明，火發，北樓陷，木石飛蔽天，守陴者皆散，賊遂入城。

translations.literal: At dawn on the ninth day, fire erupted; the north tower collapsed, wood and stone flew obscuring the sky, defenders on the ramparts all scattered, and the bandits entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the ninth, the charges detonated. The north tower collapsed, wood and stone filled the sky, the defenders on the walls fled in every direction, and the rebels poured into the city.

sentences.zh: 蜀王率妃妾自沈於菊井。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu led his consorts to drown themselves in Chrysanthemum Well.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu led his consorts and concubines to drown themselves in Chrysanthemum Well.

sentences.zh: 鎮藩突圍出，赴浣花溪死之。

translations.literal: Zhenfan broke out of the encirclement, went to Huanhua Stream and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfan fought his way out of the encirclement, made for Huanhua Stream, and died there.

sentences.zh: 之勃等被執，賊以之勃同鄉，欲用之，之勃勸以不殺百姓，輔立蜀世子。

translations.literal: Zhibo and others were captured; the bandits, seeing Zhibo was a fellow townsman, wished to employ him; Zhibo counseled them not to kill the common people and to support the heir of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibo and the others were taken prisoner. Because Zhibo was a fellow townsman, the rebels wished to put him to use; he urged them to spare the common people and install the heir of Shu as ruler.

sentences.zh: 不從，遂大罵，賊攢箭射殺之。

translations.literal: They did not listen; he then cursed loudly, and the bandits shot him to death with a volley of arrows.
translations.idiomatic: When they refused, he cursed them without restraint, and the rebels riddled him with arrows.

sentences.zh: 時福王立於南京，擢之勃右僉都御史，巡撫四川，已不及聞矣。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Fu was established in Nanjing and promoted Zhibo to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, governor of Sichuan — but it was already too late for him to hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Prince of Fu had been enthroned at Nanjing and had promoted Zhibo to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and governor of Sichuan — but the news reached him too late.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：潼關既破，李自成乘勝遂有三秦，渡河而東，勢若燎原。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Once Tong Pass was broken, Li Zicheng seized victory and gained the Three Qins, crossed the river eastward, his momentum like a spreading prairie fire.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Once Tong Pass fell, Li Zicheng rode his victory to seize the Three Qins and crossed the Yellow River eastward, his momentum spreading like wildfire across the plain.

sentences.zh: 宣、大繼覆，明亡遂決。

translations.literal: Xuan and Da fell in succession, and the fall of Ming was thus decided.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanfu and Datong followed, the doom of the Ming dynasty was sealed.

sentences.zh: 一時封疆諸臣後先爭死，可不謂烈哉！

translations.literal: At that time frontier officials vied one after another to die — can this not be called heroic!
translations.idiomatic: In that hour the frontier officials vied with one another to die for their posts — was their valor not beyond reproach!

sentences.zh: 然平陽之旆甫東，船窩之警旋告。

translations.literal: Yet scarcely had the banners turned east from Pingyang when warning came from Chuanwo.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no sooner had the banners departed Pingyang for the east than word came of disaster at Chuanwo.

sentences.zh: 死非難，所以處死為難，君子不能無憾於懋德焉已。

translations.literal: Death is not difficult; how one meets death is difficult — men of principle cannot but feel regret concerning Maode.
translations.idiomatic: To die is not the hard part; to die well is. Even men of principle cannot withhold their regret where Maode is concerned.

sentences.zh: 若夫一鶴之死顯陵，士奇之死夔州，劉之勃、龍文光之死成都，不亦得死所者歟！

translations.literal: As for Yihe dying at Xianling, Shiqi dying at Kuizhou, Liu Zhibo and Long Wenguang dying at Chengdu — did they not also meet deaths in places befitting their loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Yet if Yihe fell at Xianling, Shiqi at Kuizhou, and Liu Zhibo and Long Wenguang at Chengdu — did they not each find a death worthy of their station!
